  title: "B. A.",
  description: "Personal portfolio of B. Anderson",
There is no `template`, so every route (/, /projects, /ask, /contact, /vault, /darkroom) renders the identical `<title>B. Anderson" }`, `description: "Biomedical engineering student at Iowa State University — projects in lab-equipment repair, local LLMs, hardware, and software."` (or move BLURB/SITE_NAME into app/data/site.ts and import them). 2) Add a server `layout.tsx` next to each client page so it can export metadata without converting the page: app/projects/layout.tsx `export const metadata = { title: "Projects", description: "..." }; export default ({children}) => children;`, likewise app/ask/layout.tsx ("Ask"), app/contact/layout.tsx ("Contact"), app/vault/layout.tsx ("Vault"), app/darkroom/layout.tsx ("Darkroom"). A." — for a portfolio whose main job is being shared with recruiters this is the single most visible gap. Anderson — biomedical engineering"`, `size`, `contentType = 'image/png'`; draw the two-band motif (tan bands on #2A190D) with the name in Newsreader (fetch the .ttf via `fetch(new URL('./fonts/Newsreader.ttf', import.meta.url))` or use the Google Fonts CSS trick) and the subtitle. Anderson', url: '/', locale: 'en_US' }` and `twitter: { card: 'summary_large_image', creator: '@Bennett4Now' }` (X handle from app/data/site.ts:29). findings.title: No metadataBase or canonical URL — Vercel's inferred base may not match the www. domain used by the sitemap
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx:8-14 sets neither `metadataBase` nor `alternates.canonical`. On Vercel, Next falls back to `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL`, which Vercel documents as "the shortest production custom domain" — for this project that is `bennettanderson.com` (no www), while next-sitemap.config.js:3 declares `siteUrl: 'https://www.bennettanderson.com'` and public/robots.txt:6-9 points at the www host. Any absolute URL Next generates (og:url, og:image once added) would therefore use a different host than the sitemap, and on preview deployments it would use the *.vercel.app preview host. No page emits `<link rel="canonical">`, so the apex/www and preview duplicates are not consolidated.
findings.proposed_fix: In app/layout.tsx: `metadataBase: new URL("https://www.bennettanderson.com")` and `alternates: { canonical: "./" }` (relative canonical resolves per route in Next ≥14). Export the URL once from app/data/site.ts (`export const SITE_URL = "https://www.bennettanderson.com"`) and reference it from layout.tsx and the API User-Agent strings; next-sitemap.config.js is CommonJS so keep its literal in sync or read `process.env.SITE_URL`. Confirm in Vercel that the apex domain 301-redirects to www (or vice-versa) so canonical and sitemap agree.

findings.title: /vault and /darkroom are hidden from the sitemap but not noindexed; /darkroom is linked from the homepage so it will be indexed anyway; robots.txt allows /api/
findings.evidence: next-sitemap.config.js:8 `exclude: ['/vault', '/darkroom', '/api/*']` with the comment "meant to be found, not indexed", but sitemap exclusion does not prevent indexing. Neither page sets `robots` metadata (app/vault/page.tsx and app/darkroom/page.tsx are client components with no metadata at all, and the root metadata at app/layout.tsx:8-14 has no `robots` key). app/page.tsx:225 links `/darkroom` from every homepage render (`<TextLink href="/darkroom" arrow>More prints in the darkroom</TextLink>`), so Googlebot will crawl and index it under the title "B. A.". The generated public/robots.txt:2-3 is `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` with no Disallow, so /api/posts, /api/photos, /api/concierge/* and /api/substack are all crawlable JSON endpoints.
findings.proposed_fix: Add app/vault/layout.tsx and app/darkroom/layout.tsx (server components) exporting `metadata = { title: "...", robots: { index: false, follow: false } }` — this emits `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. In next-sitemap.config.js add `robotsTxtOptions: { policies: [{ userAgent: '*', allow: '/', disallow: ['/api/'] }] }`. Do NOT add /darkroom to robots Disallow — Google must be able to fetch the page to see the noindex; /vault can optionally be disallowed too since nothing links to it.

findings.title: Sitemap <lastmod> is stamped with build time, so the weekly health check reports SITEMAP DRIFT on every run and opens a GitHub issue each Monday
findings.evidence: next-sitemap defaults `autoLastmod: true` (node_modules/next-sitemap/dist/cjs/utils/defaults.js:66) which writes `lastmod: new Date().toISOString()` (defaults.js:46) for every URL on every build. public/sitemap.xml, sitemap-0.xml and robots.txt are committed (`git ls-files` lists all three) and regenerated by `postbuild` (package.json:12). scripts/site-health-check.mjs:31-37 runs `git diff --stat -- public/sitemap.xml public/sitemap-0.xml public/robots.txt` after the workflow's build step (.github/workflows/site-maintenance.yml:40-43, 55-58) and sets `hasIssues = true` on any diff, which makes the step fail and triggers the issue-creation step (workflow:72-77). Proof it always fires: the working tree right now, after only the baseline build, already shows `public/sitemap-0.xml | 8 ++++----` where the only change is lastmod 2026-08-29T17:33:31Z → 2026-09-03T00:21:58Z. The sitemap also declares `<changefreq>daily</changefreq>` and `priority 0.7` for all four pages, which is inaccurate for a portfolio (Google ignores both fields, but a fake daily lastmod can reduce trust in the sitemap's dates).
findings.proposed_fix: In next-sitemap.config.js set `autoLastmod: false` and `changefreq: 'weekly'` (or omit changefreq/priority entirely via a `transform` that returns only `loc`). If real lastmod values are wanted, derive them per route in `transform` from `git log -1 --format=%cI -- app/<route>/page.tsx`. Alternatively stop committing the generated files (add public/sitemap*.xml and public/robots.txt to .gitignore — Vercel regenerates them on every build) and delete the drift check from scripts/site-health-check.mjs. Either change stops the false-positive weekly issue.

findings.title: Favicon setup: SVG only, /favicon.ico 404s, no apple-touch-icon, and the SVG references a web font it cannot load — while a ready-made 512px PNG of the mark already sits unused in public/thumbnails/
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx:11-13 `icons: { icon: "/ba-favicon.svg" }` is the only icon declaration. There is no app/favicon.ico, app/icon.*, or app/apple-icon.* (ls confirms), so (a) `GET /favicon.ico` — requested unconditionally by many browsers, RSS readers, bookmark services and older crawlers — returns 404; (b) Safari (which does not use SVG favicons for tabs) and iOS "Add to Home Screen"/bookmarks get a blank/screenshot icon because there is no `apple-touch-icon`. public/ba-favicon.svg:8-9 draws the letters with `font-family="Newsreader, Iowan Old Style, Georgia, serif"`; favicon renderers cannot fetch web fonts, so the tab icon is drawn in whatever local serif exists and will not match the in-page Mark. Meanwhile public/thumbnails/favicon.png (512×512 RGBA, byte-identical to default.png — md5 1577987d…) is already a correct raster of the current BA mark and is only used as a project-card thumbnail (app/data/projects.ts:243).
findings.proposed_fix: Generate real raster icons from that PNG (or from the Mark component via `ImageResponse` in app/icon.tsx / app/apple-icon.tsx, which can embed the Newsreader .ttf so the glyph matches): `public/apple-touch-icon.png` 180×180, `app/favicon.ico` (16/32/48 multi-size), and optionally `public/icon-192.png`/`icon-512.png` plus `app/manifest.ts`. Then `icons: { icon: [{ url: '/ba-favicon.svg', type: 'image/svg+xml' }, { url: '/favicon.ico', sizes: '32x32' }], apple: '/apple-touch-icon.png' }`. Convert the text in ba-favicon.svg to outlined paths (or embed the font as a data: URI in a `<style>`) so it renders identically everywhere.

findings.title: No viewport/themeColor export and no CSS color-scheme — mobile browser chrome and native controls don't follow the brown/cream ground
findings.evidence: app/layout.tsx exports `metadata` only; there is no `export const viewport: Viewport` and therefore no `<meta name="theme-color">`, so Android Chrome's address bar and iOS Safari's tab/toolbar tint stay default grey/white above the #3A2412 / #FAF4E9 page ground (app/globals.css:64, 136). `grep -n color-scheme app/globals.css` returns nothing, so in dark mode native scrollbars, `<input type="file">` (darkroom/page.tsx:68-73), `<input type="password">` and form autofill use light UA styling on the dark surface. Next 16 injects the default width/initial-scale viewport tag automatically, so that part is fine.
findings.proposed_fix: In app/layout.tsx: `import type { Viewport } from 'next'; export const viewport: Viewport = { themeColor: [{ media: '(prefers-color-scheme: light)', color: '#FAF4E9' }, { media: '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', color: '#3A2412' }] };` and in app/globals.css add `html.dark { color-scheme: dark; } html.light { color-scheme: light; }`. Because the site's toggle can override the OS preference, also set `document.querySelector('meta[name=theme-color]')`-style updates in Navbar.toggleTheme (or a single `<meta name="theme-color">` updated by the themeInit script) so the chrome follows the actual ground.

findings.title: No structured data (Person JSON-LD) and no rel="me" on profile links
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "ld+json" app` returns nothing; the site never tells search engines that this domain is a person named Bennett M. Anderson with these GitHub/LinkedIn/YouTube/X/Substack profiles, even though all of those URLs are centralised in app/data/site.ts:3, 28-33 and the portrait is at public/profile.jpeg (app/page.tsx:117). Profile buttons (app/page.tsx:132-151) and contact rows (app/contact/page.tsx:14-15) are rendered by Button/TextLink with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` only (ui.tsx:48, 241) — no `rel="me"`, which is what GitHub, Mastodon and IndieAuth use to verify the site ↔ profile relationship.
findings.proposed_fix: In app/layout.tsx (server component) build `const person = { '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'Person', name: 'Bennett M. Anderson', url: SITE_URL, image: `${SITE_URL}/profile.jpeg`, jobTitle: 'Biomedical engineering student', affiliation: { '@type': 'CollegeOrUniversity', name: 'Iowa State University' }, sameAs: [GITHUB_URL, LINKEDIN_URL, YOUTUBE_URL, X_URL, SUBSTACK_URL].filter(Boolean) }` and render `<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(person) }} />` in <body>. Leave email/phone out of the JSON-LD to avoid making them machine-scrapable. Add an optional `rel` prop to Button/TextLink and pass `rel="me noopener noreferrer"` for the GitHub/LinkedIn/YouTube/X/Substack links.

findings.title: No custom not-found page — mistyped URLs get Next's unstyled default 404 with the tab title "404: This page could not be found."

Any unknown path (e.g. /project, /resume, old cyber-bio-era URLs) renders Next's default black-on-white centred "404 | This page could not be found." block inside the branded layout (Navbar present, everything else off-brand), and the <title> becomes Next's generic string. The status code is correctly 404, so this is a polish/professionalism issue rather than an indexing bug.

findings.title: Site identifies itself as the hyphenated domain bennett-anderson.com in fetch User-Agents and the project title, while the real site is www.bennettanderson.com

findings.title: Collapsed accordion panels stay in the tab order and accessibility tree: keyboard users tab into invisible GitHub/YouTube links and the hidden YouTube iframe
findings.evidence: The panel is collapsed purely by `grid-template-rows: 0fr` on `.md-acc-panel` (globals.css:426-437) with `overflow: hidden` on `.md-acc-inner`; the panel div in ui.tsx:280-284 has no `hidden`, `inert`, `aria-hidden` or `visibility: hidden`. On /projects every collapsed project still contains the 'View on GitHub' and 'Watch on YouTube' TextLinks (projects/page.tsx:80-88) and, for projects with videoUrl, a focusable YouTube <iframe> (projects/page.tsx:66-74). Tabbing through /projects therefore lands focus on zero-height elements with no visible focus ring, and screen readers read every collapsed project's full description. The trigger also lacks `aria-controls`/`id` pairing (ui.tsx:265-269). The same applies to SystemPanel's height:0 motion.div (SystemPanel.tsx:129-134), which is read while closed.
findings.proposed_fix: In Accordion (ui.tsx:280) give each panel an id and set `inert={!isOpen}` (React 19 supports the boolean `inert` prop; it removes the subtree from tab order and the a11y tree while letting the grid-rows transition still play), add `aria-controls={panelId}` and `id={triggerId}` on the button, and `role="region" aria-labelledby={triggerId}` on the panel. Optionally also add `visibility: hidden; transition: visibility 0s 0.28s` for the closed state in globals.css so the content is unfocusable during the closing animation. Apply `inert={!open}` to the motion.div in SystemPanel.tsx:129 as well.

findings.title: VaultGate overlay has no dialog semantics, no focus trap, no focus restore, and Escape only works once the input exists
findings.evidence: The overlay at VaultGate.tsx:518-556 is a plain `<div className="fixed inset-0 ...">` with no `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, or accessible name, so assistive tech does not know a modal opened. Escape is only handled on the password input's onKeyDown (line 544); during the ~1.05s staged boot (bootStep < 3, line 496-497) nothing is focusable and Escape does nothing. The page behind is not made inert, so Tab from the input moves focus to elements hidden under the 85% black overlay. When the gate closes (setOpen(false) at lines 520, 544) focus is dropped to <body> rather than returned to where the user was. 'access denied (n)' (line 533) is not in a live region, so a screen-reader user typing a wrong code hears nothing.
findings.proposed_fix:
Render the overlay as a native `` and call `dialogRef.current.showModal()` in the open effect (it provides top-layer rendering, focus trapping, Escape-to-close via the 'cancel' event, and `aria-modal` for free); add `aria-labelledby` pointing at the 'restricted partition' line. Save `document.activeElement` before opening and `.focus()` it on close. Wrap the denied message in `

`. If keeping the div, add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Vault access"`, move the Escape handler to a document keydown listener while open, and set `inert` on the sibling content.

findings.title: --text-faint fails contrast everywhere (3.1:1 dark, 2.3:1 light) yet is used for body-size text, error/system messages and all 11px labels
findings.evidence: Computed from the tokens: dark `--text-faint: rgba(240,220,188,0.42)` (globals.css:72) is 3.14:1 on --surface-page #3A2412, 3.31:1 on --surface-sunken, 2.88:1 on --surface-raised; light `rgba(42,25,13,0.38)` (line 144) is 2.32:1 on #FAF4E9 and 2.26:1 on the sunken ground. WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for text under 24px/18.66px-bold. It is used for 15px body text (page.tsx:209 'She answers to her name', RecentPosts.tsx:309 empty state, ask/page.tsx:310 system messages including the 'desktop is asleep' failure notice), 13px 'Connecting...' dot label, and every 11px mono kicker/label (ui.tsx:207 SectionHeading kicker, ui.tsx:182 ProgressBar label, ui.tsx:275 accordion meta/dates, contact/page.tsx:203 row labels, projects/page.tsx:151 'Sort', SystemPanel.tsx:26 stat labels, figcaptions page.tsx:218). In light mode this is below even the 3:1 large-text threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise the token alphas so faint text meets 4.5:1 on every ground it is used on. Verified values: dark `--text-faint: rgba(240, 220, 188, 0.60)` gives 4.88:1 on page / 4.28:1 on raised (raise to 0.62 if faint text is ever placed on --surface-raised); light `--text-faint: rgba(42, 25, 13, 0.65)` gives 5.08:1 on page and 4.76:1 on sunken. Keep --text-muted for hierarchy (it already passes at 5.6/4.6). Also bump light `--text-muted` (line 143) from 0.62 to 0.68 (5.2:1) because muted text over --surface-sunken in light mode (RichText <code> at RichText.tsx:352, chips on cards) is currently 4.35:1.

findings.title: Error/denial text uses --status-wip clay (#A3452A), which is 2.4-2.8:1 on the dark grounds
findings.evidence: `--status-wip: #A3452A` (globals.css:86) is meant for the 7px status dot but is used as text colour for 'access denied (n)' in VaultGate.tsx:533 and vault/page.tsx:288, and for the over-limit character counter in ask/page.tsx:431. findings.title: Vault, darkroom and VaultGate de-emphasise text with Tailwind opacity-30/40/50, which fails contrast on both grounds
findings.evidence: darkroom/page.tsx:79 uses `placeholder:opacity-30` on the access-code input (placeholder is also the only label); darkroom:93, 102, 104 and vault/page.tsx:303, 348 use `opacity-40`; darkroom:66, 101 and vault:314 use `opacity-50`; VaultGate.tsx:552 uses `opacity-40 text-xs`. Computed: opacity-40 on --text-body over the dark sunken ground is 3.37:1 and 2.31:1 in light mode; opacity-50 is 4.53:1 dark but 2.98:1 light; opacity-30 is below 3:1 on both. findings.title: /ask: the whole message log is aria-live, so the 1.5s progress ticker and the user's own message are announced; and the input is disabled while busy, which throws keyboard focus away
findings.evidence: `aria-live="polite"` is on the scrolling log container (ask/page.tsx:256), which also holds the topic-picker buttons, the echoed user message, and the busy indicator whose text changes every 1.5s via the poll (`progressLabel(progress)` at lines 371-374, seconds updated at 114-123). Separately, the composer input has `disabled={busy}` (line 394) and the submit button `disabled={busy || ...}` (line 411): when the user presses Enter the focused input becomes disabled, browsers move focus to <body>, and nothing restores it after the answer arrives, so keyboard users must Tab back through the page for every follow-up question.
findings.proposed_fix: Move `aria-live="polite"` off the container and onto a wrapper that only contains bot/system lines (or render each new bot/sys line inside `<div role="status">`), and give the busy indicator `aria-live="off"` (or `role="status"` with updates throttled to state changes rather than every second). Replace `disabled={busy}` on the input with `readOnly={busy}` (or keep it enabled and let `ask()` early-return on busy, which it already does at line 92), and after `setBusy(false)` call `inputRef.current?.focus()` via a ref on the input.

findings.title: framer-motion entrance fades on /vault and /darkroom, and the smooth-scroll on /ask, ignore prefers-reduced-motion

findings.evidence: There is no 'skip to content' link anywhere (grep for sr-only/skip returns nothing in app/), and the fixed nav is the first thing in tab order on every page. findings.title: Small naming/alt issues: 'Ask' button named 'Send question', darkroom photos use the blob filename as alt, phone number is not a tel: link

findings.title: Recent posts render a placeholder in the server HTML, then swap in the live feed after hydration (content flash + layout shift)
findings.evidence: `app/data/posts.ts` exports an empty `posts` array, so the pre-rendered HTML for `/` literally contains "// nothing published yet" (confirmed in `.next/server/app/index.html`). Only after hydration does `useEffect` (lines 56-67) `fetch("/api/posts")` and `setLive(...)`, at which point `recent` (line 69) switches from the empty file list to up to 4 YouTube/Substack cards. The YouTube channel ID is hard-coded in `/api/posts` and `YOUTUBE_URL` is set, so on production this swap happens on every cold visit: placeholder text -> ~4 cards. On viewports under 900px the rail is inline between Projects and Skills (`.md-content-split`, globals.css 251-272), so Skills and the Penrose grid jump down by several hundred pixels after the fetch lands — a visible CLS if the user has already scrolled. The comment on lines 51-53 says the file list keeps the section 'never empty on first paint', but the file is empty so that guarantee doesn't hold.
findings.proposed_fix: Fetch the feeds on the server with ISR instead of in the browser. (1) Move `youTubePosts()`, `substackPosts()` and the merge/dedupe logic out of `app/api/posts/route.ts` into a server-only module, e.g. `app/lib/posts.ts` exporting `getRecentPosts(limit)`, keeping `fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 900 } })`. (2) Make `RecentPosts` an `async` server component (drop `"use client"`, `useState`, `useEffect`) that `await getRecentPosts(limit)` inside try/catch and falls back to the manual list on error. (3) Add `export const revalidate = 900;` to `app/page.tsx` so the homepage is regenerated at most every 15 minutes with the posts already in the HTML. This requires `app/page.tsx` to be a server component (see the separate finding). `/api/posts` can then either re-export from the lib or be deleted if nothing else calls it.

findings.title: Homepage is a client component with no hooks — ships the entire projects dataset and page markup as JS
findings.evidence: `app/page.tsx` starts with `"use client"` but uses no hooks, no event handlers and no browser APIs; everything is static markup built from `publishedProjects` and site constants. Because it is a client module, the whole of `app/data/projects.ts` (19.6 KB of description text for all 9 projects, though only 3 cards are rendered) plus the page's JSX code is bundled into the homepage route chunk: `.next/static/chunks/97dc95d22f60e763.js` is 58.7 KB raw / 22 KB gzipped and contains strings like "Focus Reader" (Lit Explorer description) and "Penrose, observation". All of that is downloaded, parsed and hydrated on the landing page for no interactive benefit. It also blocks `export const metadata`/`revalidate` on the page.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `"use client"` from `app/page.tsx`. Everything it imports is compatible: `ui.tsx` primitives are already `"use client"` and receive only serialisable props (strings, style objects, ReactNode icons), `RichText` and `StripeBand` are plain components, `SkillsSection` stays a client component. Keep `XLogo`, `statusOf`, `MediaBadge`, `ProjectCard` as server functions. Expected saving on `/`: roughly the projects dataset + page code (on the order of 25-30 KB raw / ~8-10 KB gz) removed from the client bundle and less hydration work; it also enables the ISR `revalidate` export needed for the server-rendered RecentPosts fix and a per-page `metadata` export.

findings.title: YouTube embed loads the full player on /projects page load because the first accordion item is open by default
findings.evidence: `ProjectDetail` renders a real `<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/...">` for every project with a `videoUrl` (lines 63-77); the SSR HTML for `/projects` contains two such iframes (Centrifuge Repair, PiTV). `<Accordion items={items} defaultOpen={0} />` (line 160) opens the newest project — Centrifuge Repair, which has a video — so its iframe is in-viewport on load and `loading="lazy"` does nothing for it. A YouTube embed pulls ~1 MB+ of player JS/CSS and spins up a cross-origin frame before the visitor has clicked anything, which is the single largest cost on that route. The second iframe sits inside a collapsed `.md-acc-panel` (`grid-template-rows: 0fr` + `overflow: hidden`, globals.css 426-437); it is probably deferred by lazy-loading since it is clipped, but that is browser-dependent and both are always in the DOM.

findings.title: Navbar scroll-hide listens on a #scroll-panel element that no longer exists — dead on desktop, unthrottled on mobile, viewport check frozen at mount
findings.evidence: The scroll effect (lines 51-80) branches on `const isMobile = window.innerWidth < 640` computed once at mount. For non-mobile it does `document.getElementById("scroll-panel")?.addEventListener(...)` (line 74) — but `scroll-panel` appears nowhere else in the codebase (grep: only Navbar.tsx lines 57/74/78), it was part of the old two-pane layout. So on any viewport ≥640px no listener is attached and the nav never hides; on <640px it attaches to `window` and calls `setHidden` on every scroll event with no rAF/throttle. Resizing or rotating a tablet across 640px leaves the wrong listener in place until the route changes (effect deps are `[pathname]`). The `hidden` state therefore drives a `transition-all` animation that only ever runs on phones.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide whether hide-on-scroll is wanted at all (flag for the owner). If yes: delete the `isMobile`/`scroll-panel` branch and use one `window` scroll listener with `{ passive: true }`, read `window.scrollY`, coalesce with `requestAnimationFrame` (schedule one frame per burst), only call `setHidden` when the value changes, and drop `pathname` from the deps (the listener does not depend on the route). Also change `transition-all` to `transition-[transform,opacity]` so only compositor-friendly properties animate. If no: remove the effect and the `hidden` state entirely.

findings.title: Darkroom gallery renders full-size Blob originals (up to 8 MB each) through plain tags
findings.evidence: `/api/photos` POST accepts files up to `MAX_BYTES = 8 MB` and stores them as-is (`app/api/photos/route.ts` 10, 61-63). The gallery then renders each one with `` (lines 109-115, with an explicit eslint-disable for `no-img-element`). Every print is downloaded at its original resolution/bytes to fill a 2- or 3-column square thumbnail — a wall of phone photos can easily be 20-40 MB. `next.config.ts` has no `images.remotePatterns` (confirmed empty in `.next/images-manifest.json`), so `next/image` cannot currently be used for these URLs. The page is public: the homepage links to it ("More prints in the darkroom", app/page.tsx 225-227).
findings.proposed_fix: In `next.config.ts` add `images: { remotePatterns: [{ protocol: "https", hostname: "*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com" }] }`, then replace the `` with `` inside a `position: relative; aspect-ratio: 1` wrapper, and remove the eslint-disable. Optionally also lower `MAX_BYTES` or downscale on upload, but the optimizer alone brings each thumbnail to tens of KB.

findings.title: Resume preview image declares a 1:1 intrinsic size for a portrait (1632×2112) PNG — panel jumps when it loads
findings.evidence: `<Image src={p.imageUrl} width={420} height={420} style={{ width: "100%", height: "auto" }} />` (line 46) is used for `/Previews/BennettAndersonResume1.png`, which is 1632×2112 (aspect 0.77). With `height: auto` the browser reserves space from the `width`/`height` attributes (square) and then grows the box to the real ratio when the bytes arrive — at 420 px wide that is a ~123 px jump. Because the image is lazy and clipped inside a collapsed accordion, this happens exactly when the visitor opens "Resume Refresh": the panel animates open to the wrong height, then jumps again.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `next/image` the true intrinsic ratio: `width={420} height={543}` (420 × 2112 / 1632), or read the ratio from the file by importing it statically (`import resume from "@/public/Previews/BennettAndersonResume1.png"`) which also enables the blur placeholder. Add `sizes="(min-width: 640px) 420px, 100vw"` so the 2× candidate is not oversized.

findings.title: Cat photo grid has no `sizes` — 828 px images served for ~170-260 px cells
findings.evidence: `<Image src={src} width={400} height={400} style={{ width: "100%", ... }} />` with no `sizes` prop makes `next/image` emit a density srcset; the built HTML shows `srcSet="...w=640 1x, ...w=828 2x"` for every Penny image. The grid is `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4` inside a 1180 px max-width column, so cells are ~250 px on desktop and ~170 px on phones; a 2× phone therefore downloads six 828 px WebPs (from the 1600 px originals) for 170 px boxes. The 1.5 MB originals in `public/cats` are never served directly (the optimizer handles them), so the waste is per-screen oversizing, not the raw file size.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `sizes="(min-width: 640px) 25vw, 50vw"` to the cat `<Image>` (and `sizes="56px"` on the homepage thumbnails / `"34px"` on the accordion thumbnails, which are correct today but only by luck of the 1x/2x default). Also consider `images: { formats: ["image/avif", "image/webp"] }` in `next.config.ts` — the build manifest shows only WebP is enabled — for a further ~20-30% on these photos and the profile image.

findings.title: framer-motion (~36 KB gz) is loaded on /ask, /vault and /darkroom for opacity fades and one height animation that CSS already covers
findings.evidence: `.next/static/chunks/4753b301b331d3b4.js` (110 KB raw / 36 KB gz, contains framer) is included by `ask.html`, `vault.html` and `darkroom.html`. Usage: `/vault` (vault/page.tsx 4, 89) and `/darkroom` (darkroom/page.tsx 4, 55) each wrap the page in one `motion.div` fading opacity 0→1; `/ask` uses `motion.*` for fade/slide-ins (page.tsx 186-189, 224-227, 267-270, 286-294, 305-309, 318-322, 345-348) and `SystemPanel.tsx` (120-122, 129-133) animates a chevron rotate and `height: 0 ↔ auto`. `globals.css` already has `.md-acc-panel` (426-437) doing the exact open/close via `grid-template-rows`, a `prefers-reduced-motion` block (469-477) that zeroes all animation durations, and the `.md-acc-marker` rotate. `useReducedMotion` is imported only to gate these.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop framer-motion: add two keyframes to globals.css (`md-fade-in`, `md-fade-up`) and a `.md-anim-fade-up { animation: md-fade-up .3s var(--ease-out) both }` utility (stagger via inline `animationDelay`), use them on the chat panel, topic buttons and message bubbles; in `SystemPanel` reuse the `.md-acc-panel`/`.md-acc-open` grid-rows pattern and a CSS `transform: rotate(180deg)` transition for the chevron. Remove `useReducedMotion` (the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule already neutralises the CSS animations). Then `npm uninstall framer-motion`. Saves ~36 KB gz + parse/execute on `/ask`, the interactive page where TTI matters most.

findings.title: Contact page is `"use client"` with no hooks — needless client JS and no per-page metadata
findings.evidence: `app/contact/page.tsx` has `"use client"` but contains only static markup built from constants (`rows` at lines 11-16 is a plain array; no state, effects or handlers). Its route chunk `.next/static/chunks/e1091382085152df.js` (12.9 KB raw / 4.8 KB gz, contains "Context in the first") is downloaded and hydrated for a page that is entirely static. Because it is a client module it also cannot `export const metadata`, so `/contact` inherits the root title "B. A." (same problem on `/projects` and `/ask`).
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `"use client"`; `Button`/`TextLink` from `ui.tsx` are client components that accept these serialisable props, and lucide icons render as inline SVG in RSC. Then add `export const metadata = { title: "Contact — Bennett M. Anderson", description: ... }`. (Do the same on `app/page.tsx` per the earlier finding; `/projects` and `/ask` genuinely need client state, so give them a small server `page.tsx` wrapper that exports metadata and renders the client component if per-page titles are wanted.)

findings.title: /api/photos GET is uncached — every darkroom visit calls Vercel Blob `list()`
findings.evidence: `GET()` (lines 17-30) awaits `list({ prefix: "gallery/" })` on every request and returns `NextResponse.json(...)` with no `Cache-Control` and no `revalidate` export, so the route is fully dynamic (prerender-manifest lists only `/api/posts` and `/api/substack` as revalidating). The darkroom page fetches it on every mount (`darkroom/page.tsx` 16-23). Each visit pays a Blob API round-trip (~100-300 ms) before the wall appears, and Blob list operations are metered.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the listing in `unstable_cache(async () => list({ prefix: "gallery/" }), ["gallery"], { revalidate: 300, tags: ["gallery"] })` and call `revalidateTag("gallery")` at the end of `POST` after a successful `put`, so uploads appear immediately while ordinary visits are served from cache. Alternatively return `{ headers: { "Cache-Control": "public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300" } }` and have the post-upload `refresh()` call `fetch("/api/photos", { cache: "no-store" })`.

findings.title: /api/substack is dead code that still builds and deploys as a serverless function
findings.evidence: Nothing calls `/api/substack`: a repo-wide grep finds it only in a comment in `app/data/posts.ts` line 4. `app/api/posts/route.ts` already fetches and parses the same Substack RSS feed (lines 58-69) with its own copy of the tag/decode helpers. The unused route is still compiled and listed in `.next/prerender-manifest.json` with `revalidate=3600`, adds a function to every deploy, and is a second, slightly different RSS parser to keep in sync.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete `app/api/substack/route.ts` and update the comment in `app/data/posts.ts` (and the stale `/api/substack` mentions in CLAUDE.md / SITE_DOCS.md) to point at `/api/posts` or the new server-side posts lib.

findings.title: /vault renders nothing on the server (`return null` until hydration) — blank page until JS runs
findings.evidence: `if (!hydrated) return null;` (line 57) means the pre-rendered HTML for `/vault` has an empty `<main>`; the access-code form only appears after the JS bundle (including framer-motion) downloads and hydrates. The `hydrated` gate exists only to avoid reading `sessionStorage` during SSR (lines 7-10, 40-41), but the locked form itself does not depend on storage.
findings.proposed_fix: Render the gate form during SSR and only defer the *granted* branch: compute `granted = unlocked || (hydrated && sessionStorage.getItem("vault-access") === "granted")` as now, but replace `if (!hydrated) return null;` with `if (!granted) return <form…/>` so the form is in the HTML; if a returning visitor has the session flag, the unlocked view swaps in after hydration (that is the rare path). Optionally add `export const metadata = { robots: { index: false } }` via a server wrapper since the page is meant to be hidden.

findings.title: Concierge answer path issues ~120 Upstash commands per question (server poll every 700 ms + browser progress poll)
findings.evidence: `POST` LPUSHes the job then loops `await sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS /* 700 */)` + `redis(["GET", KEYS.answer(id)])` until `ANSWER_WAIT_MS = 45000` (lines 35-36, 86-103): up to ~64 GETs for one question. Meanwhile the browser polls `/api/concierge/progress?id=` every 1.5 s (`app/ask/page.tsx` 114-123) and that route issues two commands per hit (`GET progress` + `LLEN jobs`, progress/route.ts 22-25): ~60 more over a 45 s wait. A typical 10-20 s answer costs ~40-70 commands; a timeout ~125. Upstash's free tier is 10k commands/day, so a few dozen curious visitors (or one bored one) can exhaust it, after which every question fails closed as 'offline'. The serverless function also stays open for the full wait.
findings.proposed_fix: Back off the server poll: 500 ms for the first 3 s (cache hits return instantly), then 1.5 s. In `progress/route.ts`, only `LLEN` when no progress record exists yet (the queue depth is meaningless once the node is working), halving that route's cost. Move the browser poll to 2 s. Longer term, have the desktop node write the answer and progress in one `MSET`/hash and read both with a single `MGET` so each tick is one command.

findings.title: @vercel/analytics imported from `/react` instead of the Next.js entry point
findings.evidence: `import { Analytics } from "@vercel/analytics/react";` (line 6). The package (v1.5.0, confirmed in node_modules) ships a dedicated `@vercel/analytics/next` export whose component wraps the tracker in `Suspense` and derives the App Router route pattern via `computeRoute` (`dist/next/index.mjs`), which is what Vercel's dashboard uses to group pageviews and what the docs recommend for Next.js. With `/react` the tracker still works and auto-tracks client navigations, but pageviews are reported by raw path only and the component is not Suspense-isolated. Impact today is small because the site has no dynamic segments.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the import to `import { Analytics } from "@vercel/analytics/next";` (same `<Analytics />` usage). No other change needed.

findings.title: Full-page `mix-blend-mode: overlay` grain plus a fixed `backdrop-filter` navbar — worth measuring on low-end mobile
findings.evidence: The homepage wraps everything in `className="md-grain md-dapple"` (app/page.tsx 97-105), so `.md-grain::before` (globals.css 185-195: `position:absolute; inset:0; mix-blend-mode: overlay; background-image: <svg feTurbulence numOctaves=4>`) is a page-height layer blended over all content, and `.md-dapple::after` stacks seven radial-gradient layers with a mask on top of that. The fixed `<nav>` uses `backdropFilter: "blur(10px)"` (Navbar.tsx 99-101), which re-blurs the strip beneath it on every scrolled frame, and `body` carries `transition-colors duration-300`. Individually each is fine; together on the longest page they are the main per-frame GPU cost and the kind of thing that shows as dropped frames on a mid-range Android. This is unmeasured — flagging it as something to verify, not a confirmed jank.
findings.proposed_fix: Profile `/` with Chrome DevTools Performance (6× CPU throttle, mobile emulation) while scrolling. If frames drop: (a) scope the grain to the hero `<header>` only (as `/projects`, `/ask`, `/contact` already do) instead of the whole page wrapper; (b) add `contain: paint` to `.md-grain`/`.md-dapple` so their pseudo-elements don't force repaints of siblings; (c) keep the nav blur but add `will-change: transform` to the `<nav>` so it lives on its own compositor layer. Any of these is a one-line, visually identical change.

findings.title: Accordion open-state is an index, so changing the sort on /projects silently opens a different project
findings.evidence: `const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(defaultOpen ?? null)` (ui.tsx:408) and `key={i}` (ui.tsx:414); `/projects` passes `defaultOpen={0}` and rebuilds `items` from a `useMemo` that re-sorts on every sort change (projects/page.tsx:105-111, 160). The open index survives the reorder: with 'Newest' the open row is 'Video Production Workflow'; click 'Oldest' and the same slot (index 0) is now 'Bennett-Anderson.com', which appears expanded without the user touching it. Any project the user opened lower in the list likewise swaps to whatever lands at that index. Because the key is also the index, React reuses each row's DOM and just swaps content, so the YouTube iframe/thumbnail in a row is replaced in place.
findings.proposed_fix: Key rows by a stable id instead of position. Add `id: string` to `AccordionItem`, change state to `useState<string | null>(defaultOpen ?? null)` with `defaultOpen?: string`, use `key={item.id}` and `open === item.id`. On /projects pass `id: p.title` (titles are unique) and `defaultOpen={list[0]?.title}`; in SkillsSection pass `id: cat.name`. The open project then stays open under the new sort.

findings.title: Navbar scroll-hide listens on a #scroll-panel element that no longer exists — dead on desktop, and never re-evaluated on resize
findings.evidence: `grep -rn scroll-panel` finds only Navbar.tsx:57,74,78 — no element with that id is rendered anywhere. The effect decides `isMobile = window.innerWidth < 640` once per pathname (line 52), and on the desktop branch does `document.getElementById("scroll-panel")?.addEventListener(...)` (line 74), which is a no-op, and `getY()` always returns 0 (line 58). Result: the retracting nav (advertised in the site's own project description, projects.ts:218) only works below 640px; on desktop it never hides. Resizing across 640px does not re-run the effect (deps are `[pathname]`), so a narrow window widened keeps the window listener and a wide window narrowed has none. Also, when hidden the nav is only `opacity-0 -translate-y-full` (line 95) — it stays in the tab order, so keyboard users can focus invisible links.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the `scroll-panel`/`isMobile` branch and always listen on `window` (`window.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll, { passive: true })`), using `window.scrollY`. Compare against a threshold (e.g. only hide after 8px of downward delta) to avoid jitter. Add `aria-hidden={hidden}` and `inert={hidden}` (React 19 supports the boolean `inert` prop) or `visibility: hidden` after the transition so hidden links are not focusable. Alternatively, if the owner prefers a static nav, delete the effect and the `hidden` state entirely.

findings.title: Unguarded localStorage/sessionStorage reads throw during render when storage is blocked, crashing the whole app shell
findings.evidence: `readTheme()` does `localStorage.getItem("theme")` with no try/catch (Navbar.tsx:31) and is called synchronously during render via `useSyncExternalStore` (line 37). In Firefox with 'block all cookies'/`dom.storage.enabled=false`, Safari with storage blocked, and some embedded webviews, merely touching `window.localStorage` throws a SecurityError. Navbar is rendered from the root layout, so the throw takes down every page with Next's error screen. The inline boot script (layout.tsx:19) and `toggleTheme` (Navbar.tsx:86-88) are wrapped in try/catch, so the author knows storage can throw — but the render path is not. Same pattern: `sessionStorage.getItem("vault-access")` in render at vault/page.tsx:41, and `sessionStorage.setItem` in VaultGate.tsx:49 / vault/page.tsx:49.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap storage access in a small helper: `function safeGet(store: 'local'|'session', key) { try { return window[store+'Storage'].getItem(key); } catch { return null; } }` and use it in `readTheme`, vault/page.tsx:41 and both `setItem` calls. `readTheme` falls back to the matchMedia value when storage is unavailable.

findings.title: Mutually-exclusive status booleans are not exclusive: two projects render a 'complete' badge next to an 80% completion bar
findings.evidence: `Project` has five independent booleans (projects.ts:13-17). 'Local-LLM Site Concierge' sets `wip: true` AND `completed: true` with `completion: 82` (lines 110-116); 'Lit Explorer' does the same with `completion: 80` (lines 158-164). `statusOf` checks `completed` before `wip` (projects/page.tsx:11-18, duplicated verbatim at page.tsx:35-42), so both show a green 'complete' badge on the homepage and /projects directly above a progress bar reading 82%/80%. The type system cannot catch this because `Badge.status` is `string` and `statusColor` is `Record<string,string>` (ui.tsx:263, 277), and `statusOf` returns `string`.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the five booleans with `status: ProjectStatus` where `export type ProjectStatus = "wip" | "ongoing" | "complete" | "terminated" | "shelved"`; export a single `statusOf`/`statusLabel` from app/data/projects.ts and delete the two copies; type `Badge.status?: ProjectStatus` and `statusColor: Record<ProgressStatus,string>`. Migrate each entry to one value (owner to confirm: Concierge and Lit Explorer are presumably `"wip"`, given 80-82% completion). Update scripts/site-health-check.mjs only if it ever reads these fields (it does not today).

findings.title: RecentPosts flashes '// nothing published yet' on every page load before the live feed arrives
findings.evidence: `live` starts as `null` (line 54) and `recent` falls back to the hand-maintained `posts` array (line 69), which is empty (posts.ts:116-128). So the first paint (and the server HTML) always renders the 'nothing published yet' placeholder (lines 73-79); ~200-800ms later the `/api/posts` fetch resolves and three YouTube cards pop in, shifting the layout. The comment at lines 51-53 claims 'never empty on first paint', which is no longer true now that the manual list is empty.
findings.proposed_fix: Preferred: make the merge server-side. Move the YouTube/Substack merge from app/api/posts/route.ts into `app/lib/posts.ts` (`export async function getRecentPosts()` using `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 900 } })`), drop `"use client"` from app/page.tsx (it uses no hooks), make `RecentPosts` an async server component that awaits `getRecentPosts()` and passes the list into a small client `PostCard` if needed. The HTML then ships with the posts and there is no flash. Minimal alternative: while `live === null` render three low-contrast skeleton cards instead of the empty-state text.

findings.title: Homepage project cards all link to bare /projects, so clicking a specific project opens whichever project happens to be first
findings.evidence: `ProjectCard` renders `<Link href="/projects">` for every card (page.tsx:52). /projects always opens index 0 of the 'Newest' sort (projects/page.tsx:160). Clicking the second or third homepage card (e.g. 'Centrifuge Repair') lands on /projects with 'Video Production Workflow' expanded and the clicked project collapsed somewhere below — the click does not do what it visibly promises.
findings.proposed_fix: Give each project a slug (derive from title, e.g. `slugify(p.title)`) and link cards to `/projects#<slug>`. On /projects, with the id-keyed Accordion from the first finding, compute the initial open id from `window.location.hash` via `useSyncExternalStore` (subscribe to `hashchange`, server snapshot `null`, fall back to the first item) — this avoids the `set-state-in-effect` lint rule and hydration mismatch. Also give each `.md-acc-row` `id={slug}` so the browser scrolls to it, and set `scroll-margin-top` to clear the fixed nav.

findings.title: Darkroom advertises an 8 MB limit but Vercel Functions reject request bodies over 4.5 MB, so 4.5-8 MB uploads fail with 'transmission failed'
findings.evidence: `MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` (line 271) and the error copy 'file too large (8 MB max)' (line 318) are checked only after `req.formData()` (line 309). Vercel Functions cap the request body at 4.5 MB; a 5 MB phone photo never reaches this handler — the platform returns a 413 with a non-JSON body, `res.json()` throws in darkroom/page.tsx:243, and the user sees the generic 'transmission failed' (line 252) with no hint why. Most modern phone JPEGs are 3-6 MB, so this is the common case, not an edge case.
findings.proposed_fix: Either (a) lower `MAX_BYTES` to 4 MB, mirror the check client-side before upload (`file.size > 4*1024*1024` → 'file too large (4 MB max)') and fix the copy, or (b) switch to direct-to-Blob client uploads: `import { upload } from "@vercel/blob/client"` in darkroom/page.tsx and `handleUpload` from `@vercel/blob/client` in the route (`onBeforeGenerateToken` validates `x-darkroom-code`, sets `maximumSizeInBytes` and `allowedContentTypes`), which removes the size ceiling entirely. In both cases guard `res.json()` with `res.headers.get('content-type')?.includes('json')` so a platform error still produces a sensible message.

findings.title: TextLink renders internal routes as plain <a>, bypassing next/link — full page reloads for /projects, /contact, /darkroom links
findings.evidence: `TextLink` always emits a raw `<a href={href}>` (ui.tsx:387-396). It is used for in-app navigation: `href="/projects"` and `href="/contact"` on /ask (ask/page.tsx:427-428), `href="/projects"` (page.tsx:172) and `href="/darkroom"` (page.tsx:225) on the homepage. Each click is a full document navigation: no prefetch, the theme boot script and fonts re-run, and the page flashes, unlike the Navbar links which use `next/link`. `Button` with an internal `href` would have the same problem (ui.tsx:194), though today its only internal href is the PDF download.
findings.proposed_fix: In `TextLink` (and `Button`), branch on `href.startsWith("/") && !download`: render `<Link href={href} className="md-link" onClick={onClick}>` from `next/link`; keep `<a>` for http(s)/mailto/tel and for `download`. Keep the `external` target/rel logic for http only (mailto does not need `rel`).

findings.title: Every route is a 'use client' page, so no route can export metadata — all pages share the title 'B. A.'
findings.evidence: The only `metadata` export is the root layout (`title: "B. A."`, layout.tsx:8-14). app/page.tsx:1, projects/page.tsx:1, ask/page.tsx:1, contact/page.tsx:1, vault/page.tsx:1 and darkroom/page.tsx:1 all begin with `"use client"`, and a client page cannot export `metadata`/`generateMetadata`. app/page.tsx and contact/page.tsx use no hooks at all — their `"use client"` is unnecessary and also drags `publishedProjects` (all long descriptions) and the page tree into the client bundle. The browser tab, history and share previews read 'B. A.' for /projects, /ask and /contact alike; there is no `metadataBase`, `openGraph` or per-page description.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `"use client"` from app/page.tsx and app/contact/page.tsx (they render only server-safe JSX plus already-client children). For /projects and /ask, keep the interactive tree in a client component (`ProjectsClient.tsx`, `AskClient.tsx`) and make `page.tsx` a server file that exports `metadata` (`{ title: "Projects" }`, etc.) and renders the client component. In layout.tsx set `metadataBase: new URL("https://www.bennettanderson.com")`, `title: { default: "Bennett M. Anderson", template: "%s · Bennett M. Anderson" }`, a real `description`, and `openGraph`. Owner to sign off on the title strings.

findings.title: Collapsed accordion panels stay in the tab order and accessibility tree (links and YouTube iframes inside closed projects are focusable)
findings.evidence: Panels collapse purely visually via `grid-template-rows: 0fr` + `overflow: hidden` (globals.css:426-437); the content is always mounted (ui.tsx:430-434) with no `hidden`, `inert` or `aria-hidden`. On /projects that is 9 panels containing 'View on GitHub'/'Watch on YouTube' links and three `<iframe>`s. Tabbing from the first row's trigger goes through every invisible link and iframe of the closed rows, and screen readers announce all nine descriptions. The trigger also has no `aria-controls`/panel `id` pairing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `inert={!isOpen}` to the `.md-acc-panel` div (React 19 supports the boolean prop; it removes the subtree from focus and the a11y tree while keeping the CSS height animation). Give the panel `id={`${id}-panel`}` and the trigger `aria-controls` to match. Optionally set `loading="lazy"` iframes to only render when the row has been opened at least once to avoid three YouTube embeds loading on page entry.

findings.title: Nested <main> landmarks: the root layout wraps every page's own <main> in another <main>
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:34 renders `<main>{children}</main>`, and the homepage (page.tsx:160), /projects (projects/page.tsx:148), /ask (ask/page.tsx:180) and /contact (contact/page.tsx:274) each render their own `<main>` inside it. HTML allows only one visible `<main>` per document; screen readers list two nested main landmarks and the header/StripeBand sits inside the outer one.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the layout wrapper to a plain `<div>` (or a fragment) and let each page keep its own `<main>`; the comment about padding on layout.tsx:32-33 still applies to the div. Add a skip link (`<a href="#main">`) targeting the page's main while there.

findings.title: Ask page requests are not cancelled on unmount; the progress poll keeps hitting the API after navigating away
findings.evidence: `ask()` starts `setInterval` polling `/api/concierge/progress` every 1.5s (lines 114-123) and only clears it after the answer fetch settles (line 156), which can take up to 45-60s (ask/route.ts:11,35). If the visitor navigates away mid-question the interval keeps firing requests and calling `setProgress` on an unmounted component until the answer request completes. The status fetch (lines 79-84) also has no AbortController, unlike RecentPosts.tsx:57. The `history` built from `lines` (lines 126-131) is not actually stale — `busy` prevents concurrent sends — so no change is needed there.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep an `AbortController` in a ref created per question; pass its signal to both fetches; store the interval id in a ref; in a `useEffect(() => () => { controllerRef.current?.abort(); clearInterval(intervalRef.current); }, [])` cleanup abort and clear on unmount. Use the same pattern for the status fetch.

findings.title: Project dates are stored as non-ISO strings ('August 21, 2026') and sorted via Date parsing
findings.evidence: Dates like `"August 21, 2026"` (projects.ts:33,59,94,...) are parsed with `new Date(b.date).getTime()` for sorting on both /projects (projects/page.tsx:107-108) and the homepage (page.tsx:91), and `new Date(p.date).getFullYear()` for the subtitle (projects/page.tsx:115). Non-ISO date strings are implementation-defined in ECMAScript; today V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore all parse this exact format, so it works, but a typo ('Augst 21, 2026') silently becomes NaN and sorts unpredictably, and nothing in scripts/site-health-check.mjs validates the field. Posts already use ISO (`posts.ts:104-105`) with a deterministic formatter (RecentPosts.tsx:15-24).
findings.proposed_fix: Store `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` (matching `Post.date`), sort with `localeCompare`, and format for display with the same UTC `toLocaleDateString` helper used in RecentPosts (move it to a shared `app/lib/format.ts`). Add a regex check for `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/` to the health-check script.

findings.title: Dead code: /api/substack route, the VaultGate context, and Card's role=button branch are unused
findings.evidence: Nothing fetches `/api/substack` (grep shows only a comment in posts.ts:4); it was superseded by `/api/posts`, which also parses the Substack feed (posts/route.ts:384-395), yet it still deploys as a public endpoint with a second, slightly different RSS parser. `useVault`/`summonVault` (VaultGate.tsx:12-13, 30-33) are exported for a 'triple-click the DNA helix' path that no longer exists; no component consumes the context. `Card`'s `onClick`/`role="button"` branch (ui.tsx:235-253) has no callers — both usages wrap the card in a Link.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete app/api/substack/route.ts and remove the stale references in CLAUDE.md/SITE_DOCS.md. Remove the `VaultContext`/`useVault` export (keep the keystroke trigger) and the unused `onClick` path in `Card`, or leave `Card` alone if the owner wants clickable cards later.

findings.title: RecentPosts uses next/link for external YouTube/Substack URLs
findings.evidence: `<Link href={p.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` (RecentPosts.tsx:28) with fully-qualified external URLs. Next's Link detects non-local URLs and falls back to anchor behaviour, so it works, but it adds the router-aware component for no benefit and reads as a mistake next to `Button`/`TextLink`, which use `<a>` for external links.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a plain `<a href={p.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="block">`.

findings.title: framer-motion entrance animations ignore prefers-reduced-motion on the first render
findings.evidence: `useReducedMotion()` returns `null` during SSR and the first client render and only flips to `true` after an effect, so `initial={reduce ? false : { opacity: 0, y: 10 }}` (ask/page.tsx:187, 225, 268, 292) still runs the 0.35s fade/slide for reduced-motion users on page entry. The CSS override in globals.css:469-476 zeroes CSS transitions/animations but framer-motion 12 drives these via WAAPI/JS, which that rule does not affect. Same on vault/page.tsx:89 and darkroom/page.tsx:259 which don't check at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the app once in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` (a small client component rendered in layout.tsx around `{children}`), which makes framer-motion honour the OS setting globally, and drop the per-call `reduce ?` conditionals.

findings.title: SystemPanel hard-codes 'Graphics: None' even though the heartbeat reports a GPU field
findings.evidence: `<Stat k="Graphics" v="None" note="every token is computed on the CPU" />` (SystemPanel.tsx:153) is static, while `status.machine.gpu` is typed and forwarded by the status route (status/route.ts:191, 204). The same applies to the 'Model' note '3 billion parameters, 4-bit quantised' (line 151) which stays regardless of `status.model`. If the desktop node is upgraded, the panel will state facts that contradict the heartbeat sitting next to it.
findings.proposed_fix: Render `v={m?.gpu ?? "None"}` and choose the note based on presence of a GPU; derive the model note from the model string (e.g. show it only when it matches `/3b/i`) or drop it. Owner to confirm the copy.

findings.title: /api/photos POST: formData()/put() outside try/catch — any storage failure or malformed body becomes an opaque 500 and the darkroom shows "transmission failed"
findings.evidence: Lines 48 and 61 run unguarded: `const form = await req.formData();` and `const blob = await put(\`gallery/${Date.now()}-${safeName}\`, file, { access: "public" });`. `req.formData()` throws on a non-multipart body, and `put()` throws on token/quota/network errors or a pathname collision (`allowOverwrite` defaults to false). An uncaught throw makes Next return a plain-text 500 (no JSON), so `app/darkroom/page.tsx:39` `await res.json()` throws and the user sees the generic "transmission failed" instead of the reason. Every other route in the project (GET in this same file, concierge routes) wraps its I/O; POST is the one exception and it is the one with real side effects.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap lines 48–64 in try/catch. On formData() failure return `NextResponse.json({ error: "expected multipart form" }, { status: 400 })`; on put() failure log `err` server-side and return `NextResponse.json({ error: "upload failed — try again" }, { status: 502 })`. Also pass `addRandomSuffix: true` to `put()` so two same-millisecond uploads of the same filename cannot collide. In app/darkroom/page.tsx:39 guard the parse: `const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({ error: \`HTTP ${res.status}\` }));` so platform-level non-JSON errors (413, 500) surface a status instead of a catch-all.

findings.title: /api/photos: 8 MB limit is unreachable — Vercel serverless request bodies cap at 4.5 MB, so uploads between 4.5 and 8 MB fail before the route runs
findings.evidence: `const MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024; // 8 MB` and the darkroom UI does not pre-check size. Vercel rejects Serverless/Fluid function request bodies larger than 4.5 MB with a platform 413 (FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) that never reaches this handler, so the size check on line 56 only ever sees files ≤ 4.5 MB. A typical 12 MP phone JPEG is 3–6 MB, so the owner's own uploads will intermittently fail with the client's generic "transmission failed" (the 413 body is not JSON). Additionally the whole body is buffered by `req.formData()` (line 48) before `file.size` is checked (line 56), so the size limit never saves any work; the `Content-Length` header is never consulted.
findings.proposed_fix: Preferred: switch to Vercel Blob client uploads — server route uses `handleUpload` from `@vercel/blob/client` to mint a scoped token (after checking `x-darkroom-code`, restricting `allowedContentTypes` to ALLOWED_TYPES and `maximumSizeInBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, and `addRandomSuffix: true`), and the darkroom page calls `upload(file.name, file, { access: "public", handleUploadUrl: "/api/photos" })`; the file then goes browser → Blob directly with no 4.5 MB ceiling. Minimal alternative: set MAX_BYTES to 4 MB, reject early on `Number(req.headers.get("content-length")) > MAX_BYTES` before calling formData(), and mirror the limit in app/darkroom/page.tsx (`if (file.size > MAX_BYTES) { setMsg("4 MB max"); return; }`) with the copy adjusted to say 4 MB.

findings.title: DARKROOM_CODE check is a plain string comparison with no brute-force protection
findings.evidence: `if (provided !== expected) { ... 401 }`. This is documented as the site's one piece of real auth (`// real auth, unlike the vault easter egg`), yet: (a) the comparison is not constant-time (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` is one import away in a Node route), and (b) nothing throttles attempts — an attacker can hammer POST /api/photos with guesses at whatever rate Vercel accepts, and each miss is a cheap 401 before any body parsing. A successful guess grants unlimited public uploads to the site's Blob store (cost + content risk).
findings.proposed_fix: Use a length-guarded constant-time compare: `import { timingSafeEqual } from "crypto"; const a = Buffer.from(provided), b = Buffer.from(expected); const ok = a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b);`. Add rate limiting on failed attempts: either a Vercel WAF rate-limit rule on `POST /api/photos` (e.g. 10 req/min per IP — no code), or reuse the existing Upstash client with a fixed-window counter keyed by `x-forwarded-for` (`INCR darkroom:fail:<ip>` + `EXPIRE 600`, deny with 429 once ≥ 5). Recommend a DARKROOM_CODE of ≥ 20 random characters in Vercel env.

findings.title: /api/concierge/ask has no rate limiting or queue cap — anonymous flooding drains the Upstash command quota, ties up Vercel function time, and DoSes the home desktop
findings.evidence: Any POST with a non-empty `question` does `LPUSH concierge:jobs` (line 81) unconditionally, then polls `GET concierge:answer:<id>` every 700 ms for up to 45 s (lines 86–103) — roughly 65 Redis commands and 45 s of function time per question, with no per-IP limit, no cap on `LLEN concierge:jobs` before enqueuing, and no Origin/Content-Type check (a `text/plain` cross-site POST bypasses CORS preflight, so any third-party page can enqueue questions from visitors' browsers). A one-line `while true; do curl -d '{"question":"x"}' …; done` fills the queue faster than a CPU-bound 3B model can drain it, burns the Upstash free-tier command budget, and the comment on site.ts:21–22 / route line 66 says priority users "skip any request limits" — but no limits exist server-side to skip.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) Before enqueuing, read `LLEN concierge:jobs`; if it exceeds a cap (e.g. 25) and `!priority`, return `NextResponse.json({ online: true, busy: true, answer: null })` and have /ask show a "queue is full, try in a minute" line. 2) Per-IP throttle via Upstash (`INCR ask:ip:<x-forwarded-for>` + `EXPIRE 60`, deny > 5/min with 429) with `priority` exempt — this makes the "skips limits" claim true. 3) Reject requests whose `content-type` is not `application/json` with 415 (kills the no-preflight cross-site case). 4) Consider raising POLL_INTERVAL_MS to 1000–1500 ms (progress polling already gives the user feedback every 1.5 s) to cut per-question Redis commands by ~half.

findings.title: /api/posts is prerendered at build and a failed feed fetch is cached as an empty list for 15 minutes — the local build baked {"posts":[]}
findings.evidence: `export const revalidate = 900` (line 6) makes the route static-with-ISR (○ in build output; confirmed in .next/prerender-manifest.json `initialRevalidateSeconds: 900` and .next/server/app/api/posts.body = `{"posts":[]}`). `fetchFeed` swallows every failure as `null` (lines 38–41) and `youTubePosts`/`substackPosts` turn that into `[]`, so the GET returns a successful 200 with an empty array. Consequences: (a) every `next build` — including the weekly CI health check — makes live network calls to YouTube and Substack, and a transient failure at build time ships an empty feed to production until the first ISR revalidation; (b) during background revalidation a transient failure *replaces* the previously good cached response with `[]` for the next 900 s (Next only keeps the stale copy if the handler throws). Also the fetch-level `next: { revalidate }` (line 36) is redundant with the route-level export.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the route-level `export const revalidate` and add `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, keeping the per-fetch `next: { revalidate: 900 }` so Next's data cache does the 15-minute caching per feed (a thrown/failed fetch is not written to the data cache, so the next request retries immediately instead of serving an empty result for 15 min). Keep the `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=3600` header so Vercel's CDN still absorbs traffic. This also removes the build-time network dependency. Alternatively, if you prefer to stay ISR: make `fetchFeed` throw on failure and have GET rethrow when *both* feeds failed — Next then serves the last good copy — but wrap it in a `process.env.NEXT_PHASE === "phase-production-build"` guard so a build does not fail.

findings.title: /api/substack is dead code superseded by /api/posts, yet still prerenders at every build (hitting Substack) and ships as a public endpoint
findings.evidence: Grep of app/ finds no `fetch("/api/substack")` — the only references are prose in app/data/posts.ts:4 (`the Substack RSS route (\`/api/substack\`)`), SITE_DOCS.md:5 and CLAUDE.md. `app/components/RecentPosts.tsx:58` fetches `/api/posts`, which already parses the Substack feed (posts/route.ts:58–69) with a stricter parser. The dead route still exports `revalidate = 3600`, so it is prerendered on every build (a second outbound Substack request during CI) and remains a publicly reachable endpoint with its own, slightly different HTML-entity handling and the wrong User-Agent domain.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete app/api/substack/route.ts. Update the comment in app/data/posts.ts:3–5 to reference `/api/posts`, and fix the SITE_DOCS.md:5 / CLAUDE.md mention. Re-run `npm run build` so the sitemap/route manifest no longer lists it.

findings.title: Outbound User-Agent strings advertise the wrong domain (bennett-anderson.com)
findings.evidence: `"User-Agent": "bennett-anderson.com/1.0 (+https://bennett-anderson.com)"` (posts/route.ts:35) and `"User-Agent": "bennett-anderson.com feed reader"` (substack/route.ts:28). The canonical site is `https://www.bennettanderson.com` (next-sitemap.config.js:3). The hyphenated domain is not owned by the site, so the contact URL that feed operators use to identify a polite bot points at someone else's (or an unregistered) domain.
findings.proposed_fix: Change to `"User-Agent": "bennettanderson.com/1.0 (+https://www.bennettanderson.com)"` and ideally derive it from a single `SITE_URL` constant added to app/data/site.ts (which next-sitemap.config.js could also import) so the domain lives in one place.

findings.title: No security headers and X-Powered-By left on — a pentester's first-page findings
findings.evidence: `const nextConfig: NextConfig = { reactCompiler: true };` — no `headers()` and `poweredByHeader` defaults to true, so every response includes `X-Powered-By: Next.js` and lacks `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, and `Permissions-Policy`. Nothing on the site needs to be framed, and `/darkroom` accepts a password in a form, so clickjacking protection is warranted. (Vercel already adds HSTS on custom domains, so that one is covered.) There is no `middleware.ts`/`proxy.ts` or `vercel.json` setting these either.

findings.title: Feed text decoder ignores numeric character references and strips tags after unescaping
findings.evidence: `decode()` handles only `< > " " ' ' &`. YouTube Atom titles are XML-escaped and Substack RSS titles come through CDATA, but any numeric reference such as `’` (’), `'`, `é` is left verbatim in the rendered card title. The order also unescapes first and then strips `<[^>]+>` (line 22), so a title like `Why <div> is enough` loses the `<div>` text, and the nested-CDATA regex in `tag()` (line 12) returns a truncated title if a title itself contains `]]>` (rare).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a numeric-entity pass and strip tags *before* unescaping: `.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")` first, then `.replace(/&#x([0-9a-f]+);/gi, (_, h) => String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(h, 16))).replace(/&#(\d+);/g, (_, d) => String.fromCodePoint(Number(d)))`, then the named entities with `&` last. Given the feeds are tiny, this is a 4-line change; a full XML parser is not warranted.

findings.title: Upload MIME type is trusted from the client with no content sniffing
findings.evidence: `if (!ALLOWED_TYPES.includes(file.type))` checks only the browser-supplied `File.type` (set from the filename extension). A caller holding the code can label any bytes `image/png`; Blob will store and serve them with that declared content-type. Because the gallery renders them via `` and the type is image/*, this is not an XSS vector, but it does mean the "only images" guarantee is nominal and the store can accept arbitrary blobs up to the size cap.
findings.proposed_fix: Sniff the first bytes before `put()`: read `new Uint8Array(await file.slice(0, 12).arrayBuffer())` and check JPEG `FF D8 FF`, PNG `89 50 4E 47`, GIF `47 49 46 38`, WebP `52 49 46 46 … 57 45 42 50`; reject otherwise with 400. Pass `contentType` explicitly to `put()` based on the sniffed type rather than `file.type`. If you adopt client uploads (finding above), `allowedContentTypes` in `handleUpload` provides the equivalent guard.

findings.title: upstash.ts shadows the global URL constructor with an env-var constant
findings.evidence: `const URL = process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL;` rebinds `URL` for the whole module. Nothing in this file currently calls `new URL(...)`, so it works, but any future edit that does (e.g. to validate the env value or build a query) will get a confusing `URL is not a constructor` at runtime, and the shadowing is easy to miss in review.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to `const REST_URL = process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL;` / `const REST_TOKEN = …` and update the three uses in `relayConfigured` and `redis()`.

findings.title: Priority header check is safe as designed, but document that `priority` is a client-controllable flag until the rate limit exists
findings.evidence: `const priority = req.headers.get("x-concierge-priority") === CONCIERGE_PRIORITY_CODE;` — a non-constant-time equality, but since the code is intentionally in the client bundle (site.ts:20–24 documents this), timing attacks are moot and there is nothing else to exploit: the only effects are RPUSH-vs-LPUSH (queue position) and a `priority: true` field in the job that the node is said to re-validate. The one inconsistency is that both the site.ts comment and this route say priority "skips any request limits" while no server-side limits exist, so today the flag confers nothing beyond queue position.
findings.proposed_fix: No security change required. When the rate limit / queue cap from the concierge finding is added, exempt `priority` requests from it so the documented behaviour becomes true, and reword the site.ts:20–24 comment to describe exactly what priority does. Longer term, move the code to a `CONCIERGE_PRIORITY_CODE` env var read only in this route (the /ask page can then POST the typed phrase to a tiny `/api/concierge/unlock` that returns an HttpOnly cookie), which removes it from the bundle entirely.

findings.title: Contact rows overflow and get clipped on phones — email/LinkedIn/GitHub values are cut off
findings.evidence: Each contact row is a non-wrapping flex row: `display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: "var(--space-6)", padding: "var(--space-6)"` (line 35) with a fixed `width: 84, flex: "0 0 auto"` label (line 38) and the value rendered as an inline-flex `.md-link` (line 42). At 360px the row's content box is 360 − 96 (main `padding … var(--space-9)`, line 24) − 16 (card padding) − 48 (row padding) = 200px; icon 18 + gap 24 + label 84 + gap 24 leaves ~50px for the value. `bennetta32.30@gmail.com` (~170–180px, no break opportunity) cannot shrink below its min-content width, so the row overflows the card and the viewport; `overflow-x-hidden` on html/body (app/layout.tsx:26,28) then clips the tail of the address. Same for `bennett-m-anderson` and `B-M-Anderson`. This holds up to ~430px viewports, i.e. essentially every phone.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the row a grid that stacks on narrow widths: `display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 84px minmax(0,1fr)` at ≥480px and `grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0,1fr)` with the label on its own line below 480px; add `minWidth: 0` and `overflowWrap: anywhere` on the value cell (or a class like `.contact-row` in globals.css with the media query). Also apply the reduced mobile gutter from the gutter finding so the row has ~250px instead of 200px.

findings.title: Fixed 48px side gutters on phones; `--gutter-page` token exists but is never used; /ask uses a different clamp
findings.evidence: `--gutter-page: 48px` (globals.css:107) is defined but no file references it. Pages hard-code `var(--space-9)` (48px) as horizontal padding at every width: app/page.tsx:113 (`padding: "248px var(--space-9) 0"`) and :161, app/projects/page.tsx:148, app/contact/page.tsx:24. `/ask` alone uses `padding: "clamp(28px, 6vw, 64px) clamp(18px, 5vw, 48px)"` (app/ask/page.tsx:182), and darkroom/vault use Tailwind `px-6` (24px). On a 360px phone 96px (27%) of the width is gutter, leaving a 264px column; the StripeBand text uses `--stripe-inset: max(48px, …)` (globals.css:99) so on /ask the band title starts 30px to the right of the content below it.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `--gutter-page: clamp(20px, 5vw, 48px)` and `--stripe-inset: max(var(--gutter-page), calc((100vw - var(--max-width)) / 2 + var(--gutter-page)))` in globals.css; replace the horizontal `var(--space-9)` in page.tsx:113,161, projects/page.tsx:148, contact/page.tsx:24 and the clamp in ask/page.tsx:182 with `var(--gutter-page)`; use the same token in darkroom/vault when they are restyled. Band text and page content then share one left edge at every width.

findings.title: Homepage project cards are cramped at phone widths (≈136px text column)
findings.evidence: `<Card interactive style={{ display: "flex", gap: "var(--space-6)" }}>` (line 53) puts a fixed 56px thumbnail (line 54–60, `flex: "0 0 auto"`) beside the text at all widths, and `.md-card` pads 24px each side (globals.css:363). At 360px with 48px gutters the text column is 264 − 48 − 56 − 24 = 136px: the `--text-lg` (20px) title wraps to 2–3 lines, the status + media badges wrap under it, the 2-line clamped description shows ~15 characters per line, and the 240px-max progress bar is squeezed. globals.css:248-250 even documents that this card 'starts wrapping badly' under ~520px, which is exactly the mobile case.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a responsive rule for the card body: below 640px use `flex-direction: column` (thumbnail above title) or reduce to a 44px thumbnail with `gap: var(--space-4)`, and let `.md-card` pad `var(--space-5)` below 640px (`@media (max-width: 639px) { .md-card { padding: var(--space-5); } }`). Combined with the clamped gutter this yields a ~230px+ text column.

findings.title: /projects accordion: the nowrap date meta squeezes each title to ~100px on phones
findings.evidence: The accordion trigger is `justify-content: space-between` with a right group containing the meta (`whiteSpace: "nowrap"`, app/components/ui.tsx:275) and the `+` marker. `meta: p.date` (projects/page.tsx:139) is e.g. 'August 21, 2026' (~100px at 11px mono). At 360px the trigger is 264px wide; after the meta (100) + marker (~14) + two 20px gaps, the title group (34px thumbnail + gap 20 + 25px display title + two badges, line 126–136) has roughly 100px, so 'Local-LLM Site Concierge' wraps to 3–4 lines with badges stacked below. The date is repeated inside the panel ('most recently updated:', line 41), so the header copy is redundant on mobile.
findings.proposed_fix: In `Accordion` (ui.tsx:275) give the meta span a `hidden sm:inline` class (or a `.md-acc-meta` rule with `@media (max-width: 639px) { display: none }`), or move it under the title inside the left group on narrow screens. Also consider `--text-lg` for the accordion title below 640px.

findings.title: /darkroom and /vault still use the legacy terminal look instead of the MarcDesign01 system
findings.evidence: Darkroom (linked publicly from the homepage cat section, app/page.tsx:225) renders `<div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto pt-24 pb-16 px-6 font-term">` with a `> darkroom` `text-3xl font-bold` heading (line 56), opacity-based hierarchy (`opacity-50`, `opacity-40`, lines 66,93,101-104), a bare-text `[develop]` button (line 83-89), a `border-b` password field (line 79) and `rounded` (4px) gallery images (line 113) — no StripeBand header, no `.md-card`/`.md-btn`, no `--radius-lg`. /vault (page.tsx:88-91, 'THE VAULT' in `text-3xl font-bold`) and the VaultGate modal (VaultGate.tsx:79-83) do the same; globals.css:439-443 explicitly labels `.font-term` as 'legacy terminal pages … no MarcDesign01 layout yet'. Every other page opens with the two-band motif, so these read as a different site.
findings.proposed_fix: Darkroom: add the standard header (`<header className="md-grain" style={{height:232…}}><StripeBand offset="80px" title="Darkroom" subtitle="Field observations, developed on site" /></header>`), put the upload station in a `Card`, use `<Button variant="primary" size="sm">Develop</Button>`, style the code input like the /ask composer input (surface-sunken, border-subtle, radius-sm, 16px), replace `opacity-*` text with `--text-muted`/`--text-faint`, and use `--radius-lg` on gallery images. Vault/VaultGate: keep the terminal voice if desired as an easter egg, but move to tokens and `.md-card` and drop `font-bold`/Tailwind opacity classes; remove or reword the `.font-term` 'no layout yet' comment.

findings.title: Text inputs under 16px cause iOS Safari to zoom the page on focus
findings.evidence: The darkroom access-code input is `text-sm` (15px in this theme, globals.css:42) at line 79 and the file input `text-xs` (13px) at line 72; the vault input (app/vault/page.tsx:73) and VaultGate input (app/components/VaultGate.tsx:106) inherit `text-sm` from their containers (vault:62, VaultGate:83). iOS Safari zooms the viewport whenever a focused input's font-size is below 16px, and the page stays zoomed afterwards. The /ask composer already avoids this with `fontSize: 16` (app/ask/page.tsx:403).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a global rule in globals.css: `input, textarea, select { font: inherit; font-size: max(1em, 16px); }` (keeps desktop sizing, prevents mobile zoom), and drop the per-input `text-sm`/`text-xs` sizes.

findings.title: Navbar tap targets are below 44px and the link strip has no overflow affordance on very narrow phones
findings.evidence: The theme toggle is `p-2` around a 17px icon (line 142-145) → 33×33px. Nav links are bare text with `pb-0.5` (line 126) → ~20px tall hit areas. Below ~345px (iPhone SE 1st gen, folded devices) the fixed-width content (mark 26 + px-4 + 4 links ≈ 229px + toggle 33 + gaps) exceeds the viewport, so the `overflow-x-auto no-scrollbar` strip (line 119, globals.css:446-452) silently hides 'Contact' with no scrollbar or fade to signal it scrolls.
findings.proposed_fix: Give links `py-2.5 min-h-11 flex items-center` and the toggle `min-w-11 min-h-11 -my-1.5 flex items-center justify-center` (keeps the nav's flow height). For the strip, either drop to `gap-3` below 400px and `text-xs` links, or add a right-edge fade via `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black calc(100% - 16px), transparent)` when it overflows.

findings.title: Navbar scroll-hide targets a `#scroll-panel` that no longer exists, so behaviour differs by width and never updates on resize
findings.evidence: `const isMobile = window.innerWidth < 640` is captured once per pathname (line 52). On ≥640px, `getY()` reads `document.getElementById("scroll-panel")?.scrollTop ?? 0` (line 57-58) and the listener is attached to that element (line 74); no page renders `#scroll-panel` any more (the old homepage right column), so on desktop the nav never hides and the listener is a no-op.
