On <640px it hides on scroll-down. Rotating a phone or resizing keeps the stale branch. SITE_DOCS.md:48,72 still describe the removed element.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the `isMobile`/`scroll-panel` branches and listen to `window` scroll on every width (or remove the hide behaviour entirely for a simpler, more predictable fixed bar — the owner should choose). Use `{ passive: true }` on the listener. Update SITE_DOCS/CLAUDE.md accordingly.

findings.title: No `color-scheme` for the class-based theme — native scrollbars and form controls render in light UA style on the dark ground
findings.evidence: The `html` rule (lines 165-168) and the `html.light`/`:root` token blocks never set `color-scheme`, and no `<meta name="theme-color">`/`viewport.themeColor` is exported in app/layout.tsx. Result in the default dark theme: the /ask message log (`overflowY: "auto"`, app/ask/page.tsx:262-263) shows a bright white scrollbar track on Windows/Linux Chrome, the darkroom `<input type="file">` (darkroom/page.tsx:72) and password autofill styling use light UA colours, and mobile browser chrome stays white above a #3A2412 page.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `html.dark { color-scheme: dark; } html.light { color-scheme: light; }` under the theme blocks in globals.css (default `:root { color-scheme: dark; }` to match the dark-first tokens), and export `viewport: { themeColor: "#3A2412" }` from layout.tsx, updating the meta tag from `toggleTheme` in Navbar (`document.querySelector('meta[name=theme-color]').setAttribute('content', next==='dark' ? '#3A2412' : '#FAF4E9')`).

findings.title: `--text-faint` is below 3.5:1 in dark mode and ~2.3:1 in light mode, and is used for readable copy
findings.evidence: Dark: `--text-faint: rgba(240,220,188,0.42)` (line 72) on `--surface-sunken` #2A190D ≈ 3.3:1. Light: `rgba(42,25,13,0.38)` (line 144) on #FAF4E9 ≈ 2.3:1 (computed). It is used not only for 11px uppercase kickers (ui.tsx:180-184, 205-209) but for sentence copy: the Penrose intro 'She answers to her name. Type it anywhere.' (app/page.tsx:210, `color: "var(--text-faint)"`), the /ask system messages (ask/page.tsx:310), figcaptions (page.tsx:218) and progress labels. Light-mode users get noticeably worse legibility than dark-mode users, so the two grounds are not at parity.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise light `--text-faint` to `rgba(42,25,13,0.55)` (~3.6:1) and dark to `rgba(240,220,188,0.5)` (~3.9:1) so both grounds sit above 3:1 for the small mono labels; switch sentence-length copy (page.tsx:210, ask/page.tsx:310) to `var(--text-muted)` (6.2:1 dark / 4.6:1 light).

findings.title: No print stylesheet — the dark theme prints cream text on white paper
findings.evidence: The comment at line 133 says the eggshell tokens are for 'Print and any .md-light box', but there is no `@media print` block anywhere; `.md-light` is also unused in the app. With the default dark tokens, browsers that skip background graphics (Chrome/Edge default) print `#F5EBDA` body text on white, and the fixed Navbar (Navbar.tsx:94) and grain/dapple pseudo-elements print on every page.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `@media print { :root { /* copy of the html.light token block */ } nav { display: none } .md-grain::before, .md-dapple::after { display: none } a { color: inherit } }`. To avoid duplicating the token list, move the light values into a `@mixin`-free pattern: put the light block selector list as `.md-light, html.light` today and add a second copy under `@media print { :root {…} }` (17 lines).

findings.title: `overflow-x-hidden` on html/body is justified by a removed DNA strip, blocks `position: sticky`, and the 100vw stripe inset misaligns by half a scrollbar
findings.evidence: `overflow-x-hidden` is on both `<html>` (line 26) and `<body>` (line 28). globals.css:241-246 explains it is 'load-bearing for the mobile full-bleed DNA strip' — that component no longer exists and nothing in app/ sets `width: 100vw`. Because `overflow-x: hidden` makes body a scroll container, the same comment notes sticky can never engage (the rail therefore isn't sticky). Separately `--stripe-inset: max(48px, calc((100vw - 1180px) / 2 + 48px))` (globals.css:99) uses `100vw`, which includes the scrollbar, so on Windows/Linux the band title sits ~7–8px right of the content column's left edge.
findings.proposed_fix: Change html/body to `overflow-x: clip` (no scroll container, sticky works, still guards against stray overflow) and rewrite the globals.css:241-246 comment. For the inset, compute from the layout width instead of 100vw: render the band text inside a nested `max-width: var(--max-width); margin: 0 auto; padding-inline: var(--gutter-page)` wrapper in StripeBand and drop `--stripe-inset`.

findings.title: Penrose photo grid: 6 photos in 4 columns leaves a ragged 4+2 last row on tablet/desktop
findings.evidence: `<div className="grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4" …>` (line 212) with six `catPhotos` entries (lines 26-33) fills 2×3 on phones but 4+2 from 640px up, so the section ends with a half-empty row under the 'Selected work' column.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3` (2×3 → 3×2, always full) — the main column is ~724px at 1180px so each tile is ~215px, still a good size.

findings.title: Theme toggle flips surfaces at different speeds because only `<body>` has a colour transition
findings.evidence: `<body className="… transition-colors duration-300">` (line 28) animates body's background/colour over 300ms, but `html` (globals.css:165-168), every page header (`background: var(--surface-sunken)`, e.g. projects/page.tsx:145, ask/page.tsx:175), cards and the Navbar (`color-mix(... var(--surface-page) …)`, Navbar.tsx:98) change instantly. On /projects, /contact and /ask the header and Navbar snap while the main area below fades, producing a visible two-tone frame during the toggle.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove `transition-colors duration-300` from body, or apply one consistent rule such as `html, body, .md-card, header, nav { transition: background-color .3s var(--ease-standard), color .3s var(--ease-standard) }` (already zeroed under `prefers-reduced-motion`).

findings.title: Homepage band offset (104px) and 248px hero top differ from the 80px used on every other page, adding dead space on phones
findings.evidence: Homepage: `<StripeBand offset="104px" …>` (line 110) and content `padding: "248px …"` (line 113). Projects/contact/ask: `offset="80px"` inside a 232px header. The Navbar is the same ~57px on every route, so the bands sit 24px lower on the home page only. On a 360×640 phone that means ~47px of empty ground between nav and band, and the profile image (188px, line 116-122) plus 248px of top padding push the blurb to ~y=436px, so first paint shows only name + photo.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `offset="80px"` and `padding-top: 224px` on the homepage to match the subpages (or make both fluid: `offset={"clamp(72px, 12vw, 104px)"}` and `padding-top: calc(offset + 144px)`), and consider a smaller profile image on phones (`width: clamp(120px, 40vw, 188px)`).

findings.title: Nested `<main>` landmarks on every page
findings.evidence: The root layout wraps children in `<main>{children}</main>` (line 34) and every page renders its own `<main>` inside it: app/page.tsx:160, app/projects/page.tsx:148, app/contact/page.tsx:24, app/ask/page.tsx:180. Two main landmarks per document confuses screen-reader landmark navigation and is flagged by axe.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the layout wrapper to a plain `<div>` (or remove it) and keep the page-level `<main>`; alternatively keep the layout `<main>` and turn the page ones into `<section>`/`<div>`.

findings.title: Mark hard-codes hex colours and depends on a `tone` prop, so it can't follow the theme tokens and flips after hydration for light-mode users
findings.evidence: Ground/letter/ring/band colours are literal hex values chosen by `tone` (lines 28-35, 72, 90) rather than the semantic tokens the rest of the design uses. Navbar passes `tone={dark ? "dark" : "light"}` (Navbar.tsx:107) from `useSyncExternalStore` whose server snapshot is `"dark"` (Navbar.tsx:37), so a light-theme visitor's first paint has a dark-tone mark that swaps to light after hydration. The lockup variant's name colour also mixes a literal `#2A190D` with `var(--text-strong)` (line 90).
findings.proposed_fix: Drive the SVG from CSS variables so it follows `html.light` with no prop and no hydration flip: e.g. `fill="var(--mark-ground)"`, `fill="var(--mark-letter)"`, `stroke="var(--mark-ring)"`, with `--mark-*` defined next to the other tokens in globals.css for both grounds. Keep `tone` only as an explicit override for the favicon export.

findings.title: No custom 404 page or error boundary — a bad URL drops visitors onto Next's stock white error screen
findings.evidence: `find app -name 'not-found*' -o -name 'error*' -o -name 'loading*'` returns nothing. Any typo'd URL (e.g. /project, /resume) renders Next's built-in not-found, whose inline-styled black-on-white "404 | This page could not be found" sits inside the brown MarcDesign01 layout with the navbar above it. Likewise an uncaught render/runtime error in any client page (`/ask`, `/darkroom` both fetch on mount) has no `error.tsx`, so the visitor gets the framework's default error screen with no way back into the site.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `app/not-found.tsx` built from the existing primitives: the same `<header className="md-grain" style={{height:232}}>` + `<StripeBand offset="80px" title="404" subtitle="Nothing lives at this address" />` pattern used by /projects, /ask and /contact, followed by a `<main className="md-dapple">` with a one-line explanation, a `<Button variant="primary" href="/">Back home</Button>` and `TextLink`s to /projects and /contact. Add `app/error.tsx` (`"use client"`, `({ error, reset }) => ...`) with the same shell, title "Something broke", and a `<Button onClick={reset}>Try again</Button>`. Both are new pages so they need no changes to existing routes. (A `loading.tsx` is not worth adding: every page is a client component with static data; only /ask and /darkroom fetch, and they already render their own skeleton states.)

findings.title: Homepage project cards all link to /projects generically instead of opening the project that was clicked
findings.evidence: `<Link href="/projects" ...>` is the same for all three cards (`recentProjects.slice(0, 3)`), so clicking "Lit Explorer" lands the visitor at the top of /projects with whichever item is at index 0 open (`<Accordion items={items} defaultOpen={0} />`, app/projects/page.tsx:160). The card looks like a link to *that* project — its hover border warms (`.md-card-interactive:hover`) — but the visitor then has to find it again in a 9-item accordion.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) Add a `slug` to each project (derive in `app/data/projects.ts`: `export const slugOf = (p: Project) => p.title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-|-$/g, '')`). 2) Homepage card: `href={`/projects#${slugOf(p)}`}`. 3) Extend `AccordionItem` with `id: string`, render `<div id={item.id} className="md-acc-row" style={{ scrollMarginTop: 96 }}>` (clears the fixed navbar), and let `Accordion` take an optional controlled `open?: string | null` / `onOpenChange` keyed by `id` (see the next finding — the index-based state is the same root cause). 4) In `ProjectsPage`, read the hash with `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeHash, () => window.location.hash.slice(1), () => "")` (matches the repo's lint rule against setState-in-effect), use it as the initial open key, and after mount `document.getElementById(hash)?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })`. The `#hash` also becomes a shareable per-project URL, which recruiters actually use.

findings.title: Projects accordion tracks the open panel by array index, so re-sorting silently switches which project is expanded; sort buttons have no toggle semantics
findings.evidence: `const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(defaultOpen ?? null)` keys the open panel by position. `ProjectsPage` rebuilds `items` in a new order on every sort change (app/projects/page.tsx:105-111) but the `Accordion` keeps `open = 3`, so after a visitor expands "PiTV" and clicks "Oldest", a different project is suddenly the one expanded and PiTV is collapsed — with no animation cue, because both rows keep their `key={i}`. The sort buttons (app/projects/page.tsx:154-158) are plain `<Button>`s: the selected one is only distinguished by colour, there is no `aria-pressed`, and the row is not a labelled group, so a screen reader hears three unrelated buttons named Newest/Oldest/Most complete.
findings.proposed_fix: In `Accordion`, key state by a stable id: `items: (AccordionItem & { id: string })[]`, `useState<string | null>(defaultOpen ?? null)`, `key={item.id}`, `isOpen = open === item.id`. `SkillsSection` passes `id: cat.name`; `ProjectsPage` passes `id: slugOf(p)` and `defaultOpen={slugOf(list[0])}` (or the hash from the previous finding). Then the same project stays open across sorts and moves with its row. For the buttons: add `"aria-pressed"?: boolean` (and generally `...rest` for aria-* props) to `ButtonProps` and forward it to the `<button>`; wrap the row in `<div role="group" aria-label="Sort projects">` and pass `aria-pressed={sort === k}`.

findings.title: Navbar hide-on-scroll listens to a #scroll-panel element that no longer exists, so behaviour differs by viewport and the hidden nav stays in the tab order
findings.evidence: Lines 55-59 and 73-78: on viewports >= 640px the handler is attached to `document.getElementById("scroll-panel")`, but `grep -rn scroll-panel app` finds no element with that id anywhere in the redesigned pages — it was the old homepage's internal scroller. Result: on desktop the nav never hides; on phones it hides on scroll-down. `isMobile` is also computed once per pathname (line 52), so rotating a tablet or resizing keeps the wrong branch. When hidden the nav is only `opacity-0 -translate-y-full` (line 95): its four links and the theme toggle remain focusable, so a keyboard user Tab-ing from the page jumps into an invisible bar. Separately, the active link (lines 121-133) is marked only by colour/underline — no `aria-current="page"`.
findings.proposed_fix: Either drop the hide-on-scroll entirely (simplest, and a fixed 52px bar is not intrusive on any page here), or make it consistent: delete the `isMobile`/panel branch and always use `window.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll, { passive: true })` reading `window.scrollY`. If kept, add `aria-hidden={hidden}` and `pointer-events-none` + `invisible` (Tailwind `visibility:hidden`, which also removes it from the tab order) while hidden, applied after the transition via `transition-[opacity,transform,visibility]`. Add `aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}` on the active `<Link>`.

findings.title: Contact page phone number is plain text, not a tel: link; LinkedIn handle is hard-coded separately from LINKEDIN_URL
findings.evidence: `{ icon: <Phone size={18} />, label: "Phone", value: CONTACT_PHONE }` has no `href`, so it falls into the non-link branch (line 44) and renders as a `<span>`. On a phone — the device most likely to be used to call — the number cannot be tapped, while the email row on line 12 is a `mailto:`. The copy above (line 27) explicitly invites calling. Line 14 hard-codes `value: "bennett-m-anderson"` while the href comes from `LINKEDIN_URL` in site.ts; if the URL changes the displayed handle silently goes stale.
findings.proposed_fix: Line 13: `{ icon: <Phone size={18} />, label: "Phone", value: CONTACT_PHONE, href: `tel:${CONTACT_PHONE.replace(/[^\d+]/g, "")}` }` (yields `tel:8158219604`). `TextLink` already treats non-http hrefs as same-tab, so nothing else changes. Line 14: derive the handle, e.g. `value: new URL(LINKEDIN_URL).pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean).pop() ?? LINKEDIN_URL`. Optional polish: a small copy-to-clipboard button on the email row (`navigator.clipboard.writeText`) with a 1.5s "copied" state — recruiters paste addresses into ATS tools more often than they click mailto.

findings.title: Darkroom upload: no form, so Enter in the code field does nothing; busy state and messages are ambiguous
findings.evidence: Lines 67-90 are a bare `<div>` with a file input, a `<input type="password">` and a `<button onClick={upload}>` — there is no `<form>` and no `onKeyDown`, so typing the code and pressing Enter (the natural gesture, and the one the vault gate supports on line 131 of app/vault/page.tsx) does nothing. While uploading, only the button is disabled (line 85); the file and code inputs stay editable, so the user can swap the file mid-upload. Line 30 sets the upload message to `"developing…"` and line 102 shows the identical `"developing…"` for the initial gallery fetch, so on a slow connection two identical strings mean two different things. If `/api/photos` GET returns `{ configured: true, photos: [], error: "list failed" }` (route line 246) the page shows `[ the wall is bare ]` — an empty gallery rather than a failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap lines 67-90 in `<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); upload(); }}>` and make the button `type="submit"`; add `disabled={busy}` to both inputs and `aria-busy={busy}` on the form. Use distinct copy: keep `"developing…"` for the upload and change line 102 to `"loading prints…"`. In `refresh`, keep `data.error` in state and render `"// couldn't reach the wall — try again"` when set instead of the bare-wall line. Also give `refresh` an `AbortController` and return its abort from the effect (line 23) so a fast navigate-away doesn't set state on an unmounted page.

findings.title: Darkroom prints can't be opened full-size and use the raw blob filename (with timestamp prefix) as alt text
findings.evidence: Each photo is a bare `` — square-cropped thumbnails with no click target, so a visitor cannot see the uncropped image at all. `alt={photo.pathname.replace("gallery/", "")}` yields strings like `1725000000000-IMG_4021.jpeg` (the route names blobs `gallery/${Date.now()}-${safeName}`, route line 279), which is what screen readers will read aloud.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each image in `<a href={photo.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" aria-label={`Open print ${i + 1} full size`}>` (a lightbox would be nicer but a new-tab open fits the site's restraint and needs no dependency). Set `alt={`Darkroom print ${i + 1}`}` and, if the owner wants dates, show `new Date(photo.uploadedAt).toLocaleDateString()` in a `<figcaption>` matching the homepage cat grid's mono captions.

findings.title: /vault and /darkroom still use the pre-redesign terminal styling and don't match the rest of the site
findings.evidence: Both pages open with `<div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto pt-24 pb-16 px-6 font-term">` (darkroom line 54; vault page lines 120 and 147 with `pt-28`) — monospace body text, `> darkroom` / `> cat currently.log` prompts, `[develop]` bracket buttons, Tailwind `opacity-*` classes — while every other page uses the `md-grain` header + `StripeBand` + `md-dapple` main pattern and the `ui.tsx` primitives. `app/globals.css:439` still says "legacy terminal pages (/ask, /vault, /darkroom) ... have no MarcDesign01 layout yet", but /ask has since been redesigned. A visitor arriving at /darkroom from the homepage's "More prints in the darkroom" link (app/page.tsx:265) gets a visibly different site. The darkroom also shows the password/upload station to every visitor even though only the owner can use it.
findings.proposed_fix: Give both pages the shared shell: `<header className="md-grain" style={{height:232}}><StripeBand offset="80px" title="Darkroom" subtitle="Field observations, developed on site" /></header>` and `<main className="md-dapple" style={{maxWidth:"var(--max-width)", margin:"0 auto", padding:"var(--space-9) var(--space-9) var(--space-11)"}}>`, replacing `[develop]` with `<Button variant="primary">Develop</Button>` and the bracketed empty state with the `text-faint` style used by `RecentPosts`. Tuck the upload station behind a small `TextLink` ("Keeper's entrance") that toggles it, so first-time visitors see a gallery, not a login. The vault can keep its monospace flavour intentionally (it's an easter egg), but should at least drop `pt-28`/`pt-24` in favour of the same header band. Update the globals.css comment on line 439. This is a design change — owner to confirm the darkroom tone.

findings.title: /ask: status is fetched once and never refreshed, offline visitors can still wait the full 45s, and disabling the input on send drops focus and the mobile keyboard
findings.evidence: Lines 79-84 fetch `/api/concierge/status` exactly once on mount. The node's heartbeat TTL is ~30s (status route comment), so a visitor who leaves the tab open sees a stale "Online"/"Offline" pill indefinitely, and after an answer fails closed the pill can still say Online. When the pill says "Offline — the desktop's asleep" (line 167), the composer is fully enabled; a question is still enqueued and the ask route polls for `ANSWER_WAIT_MS = 45000` (app/api/concierge/ask/route.ts:35) before returning `answer: null`, so the visitor watches "waiting for the desktop to pick it up…" for 45 seconds before the "asleep" message on line 149. Line 394 (`disabled={busy}` on the `<input>`) means every send blurs the field: on iOS the keyboard dismisses, and after the answer arrives nothing restores focus, so each follow-up requires tapping the box again.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) Extract the status fetch into a `loadStatus` function, call it on mount, on a `setInterval(loadStatus, 30000)` (cleared on unmount, paused when `document.hidden`), and again after every `ask` resolves. 2) When `status && !status.online && empty`, render a `sys`-style line in the empty state above the topic chips: "The desktop is asleep right now — questions will wait up to 45 seconds, then give up. Projects and Contact still work." and set the placeholder to "The desktop is asleep — ask anyway". Keep sending allowed (the node may wake), but the wait is now explained. 3) Replace `disabled={busy}` on the input with `readOnly={busy}` (keeps focus and keyboard), guard submission with the existing `if (!q || busy) return` (line 92), and add `const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)` + `inputRef.current?.focus()` at the end of `ask` for the desktop case.

findings.title: Buttons have no :disabled style — the send button fakes it with inline opacity and the topic chips show no disabled state at all
findings.evidence: `.md-btn` (lines 284-335) defines hover/active but no `:disabled` rule, and `cursor: pointer` remains on disabled buttons. The /ask send button works around this inline: `style={{ opacity: busy || input.trim().length === 0 ? 0.5 : 1, minHeight: 44 }}` (app/ask/page.tsx:413). The topic chips are `<motion.button disabled={busy} className="md-btn md-btn-secondary md-btn-sm">` (app/ask/page.tsx:290-296) and look identical enabled or disabled. `.md-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px) }` also fires on a disabled button in some browsers since nothing gates it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to globals.css after `.md-btn-sm`: `.md-btn:disabled, .md-btn[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; pointer-events: none; }` and change `.md-btn:active` to `.md-btn:not(:disabled):active`. Remove the inline `opacity` from the send button (keep `minHeight: 44`).

findings.title: Vault gate overlay: Escape only works once boot finishes, no dialog semantics, and the 'access denied' counter persists between summons
findings.evidence: The Escape handler is on the `<input>` (line 104), which is only mounted after `bootStep >= BOOT_LINES.length` (~1.05s of staged lines, line 57). During boot the only way out is clicking the backdrop (line 80) — pressing Esc, the universal dismiss, does nothing. The overlay has no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, so assistive tech treats it as ordinary page content, and page scrolling behind it isn't locked. `summonVault` (lines 30-34) resets `bootStep` and `input` but not `denied`, so a second summons opens straight to "access denied (2)" from an earlier attempt. Focus is not returned to the previously focused element on close.
findings.proposed_fix: Move Escape to a window listener active while `open` (in the existing keydown effect: `if (open && e.key === "Escape") { setOpen(false); return; }` before the `if (open) return`). Add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Vault access"` to the inner panel, `document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"` while open (restore on close), and `setDenied(0)` in `summonVault`. Store `document.activeElement` on open and `.focus()` it on close. Backdrop-click-to-close can stay — it's the expected behaviour for a modal.

findings.title: Homepage tells visitors to type the cat's name 'anywhere', but under the heading 'Penrose' — and typing 'penrose' never triggers the vault
findings.evidence: The section heading is "Penrose" (line 248) and the hint reads "She answers to her name. Type it anywhere." (line 250). The trigger is `VAULT_TRIGGER = "penny"` (app/data/site.ts:10) and the buffer only keeps the last `VAULT_TRIGGER.length` = 5 characters (VaultGate.tsx:43), so a visitor who does exactly what the hint says and types `penrose` ends up with a buffer of `nrose` and nothing happens. The name "Penny" appears nowhere on the homepage — only inside the vault itself (app/vault/page.tsx:84). A first-time visitor who follows the only clue can't find the easter egg.
findings.proposed_fix: Code-only fix that keeps the owner's copy: make the trigger a list in site.ts — `export const VAULT_TRIGGERS = ["penny", "penrose"]` — and in VaultGate keep `Math.max(...VAULT_TRIGGERS.map(t => t.length))` characters, checking `VAULT_TRIGGERS.some(t => buffer.current.endsWith(t))`. Update `CLAUDE.md`'s vault note to match. (Alternative if the owner prefers: change line 250 to mention Penny, e.g. "Her friends call her Penny. Type it anywhere." — copy change, owner's call.)

findings.title: Stale terminal-era strings survive in UI: vault hint references the removed DNA helix, and RecentPosts uses a '//' comment placeholder
findings.evidence: Vault gate hint (line 139): "hint: the cat guards this. ask the machine about her, or read the strands." — "the strands" pointed at the old ASCII DNA helix (`AsciiDna.tsx`, no longer in the repo), so the second half of the hint now leads nowhere. `app/components/RecentPosts.tsx:76` renders `{"// nothing published yet"}` — a code-comment prefix from the old cyber-terminal design sitting under a serif "Recent posts" heading in the new one. `VaultGate.tsx:8` comment still mentions "triple-clicking the DNA helix" and exports `useVault` that nothing imports (`grep useVault app` shows only its definition).
findings.proposed_fix: Line 139: drop the helix clause — e.g. "hint: the cat guards this. ask the machine about her." (the /ask concierge grounding doc does cover Penny). RecentPosts line 76: "Nothing published yet — check the channels below." in the same `text-faint` style. Update the VaultGate comment and either remove the unused `useVault` export or leave it with an accurate comment. All three are copy tweaks for the owner to confirm.

findings.title: RichText renders the '~(' note prefix literally and leaves bare URLs unclickable
findings.evidence: `TOKEN` only handles `**bold**`, `*italic*` and `` `code` ``. Four project descriptions use a `~(...)` convention for footnotes — `~(Thumbnail illustration by DataBase Center...)` (projects.ts:32), `~(Written to make my own videos...)` (185), `~(Section update & video demo coming soon)` (256), `~photos and build process coming soon!` (279) — which the old site presumably styled as a muted aside; today the tilde renders as a literal `~(` in the visitor's face on both the homepage card (2-line clamp) and the /projects panel. The Centrifuge description embeds `https://youtu.be/f-lBA9Kq3T4?si=uDx0hGnT-V_UUTgt` as plain text (projects.ts:30) that cannot be clicked, and the tracking `?si=` param is shown verbatim.
findings.proposed_fix: In `RichText`, split on lines first: a line that starts with `~` renders as `<span style={{ display:'block', fontSize:'var(--text-xs)', color:'var(--text-faint)' }}>` with the tilde stripped (keeping the `(...)`), and other lines pass through the existing inline tokenizer. Add a URL token to `TOKEN` (`|https?:\/\/[^\s)]+`) rendered as `<a href className="md-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` showing the hostname+path without the query string. On the homepage card, filter out `~` lines before clamping so the 2-line preview is prose. No data edits needed for the convention itself; the `?si=` tracking param in projects.ts:30 can be dropped by the owner.

findings.title: Two projects are flagged both wip:true and completed:true — the badge reads 'complete' next to an 80%/82% completion bar
findings.evidence: Local-LLM Site Concierge (lines 112-116: `wip: true ... completed: true`, `completion: 82`) and Lit Explorer (lines 160-164, `completion: 80`). `statusOf` in both app/page.tsx:75-82 and app/projects/page.tsx:11-18 checks `completed` before `ongoing`/`wip`, so both render a moss-green "complete" badge directly above a progress bar at 82% / 80%, and the Concierge description itself ends with "I'm working to improve this". `scripts/site-health-check.mjs` has no status-flag validation, so nothing catches this. ("Video Production Workflow" sets `wip` and `ongoing` both true, which resolves to "ongoing" and is harmless.)
findings.proposed_fix: Content decision for the owner: set `completed: false` on both (badge becomes "wip", matching the bar), or raise `completion` to 100 if they are considered done. Code hardening regardless: dedupe `statusOf` into `app/data/projects.ts` and have it prefer `wip`/`ongoing` over `completed` when `completion < 100`; add an assertion to `site-health-check.mjs` that at most one of `completed|terminated|shelved` is true and that `completed` implies `completion === 100`.

findings.title: Obvious typos and broken line-wrapping in project descriptions (rendered verbatim with white-space: pre-line)
findings.evidence: Spelling: "dissasembled" (27), "youtube videos" (27), "all thats needed to steam anything" → "that's ... stream" (50), "accessability" (52), "theres a sleep timer", "the pi", "stop the steam", "dont" (56), "art intallation" (58), "indefinetly" (92), "textscript website development" → "TypeScript" (223), "in the future!." (254), "demonstate" (299), "using using" (300). Formatting: /projects renders descriptions with `whiteSpace: "pre-line"` (app/projects/page.tsx:49), so single newlines become hard breaks — the MP3 Merger text breaks mid-sentence after "crossfades**," (253→254), Resume Refresh after "document class," (300→301), and Bennett-Anderson.com puts each sentence on its own line (216-218); line 299 also has 4 leading spaces. The double space in "testing,  capacitor" (27) is collapsed and harmless.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix only the mechanical errors listed (spelling, doubled words, "!.", the mid-sentence newlines joined with a space) — no rewording of the owner's prose. Present the exact before/after for each line for sign-off since this is the owner's voice.

findings.title: No site footer — pages end abruptly with no copyright, source link, or secondary navigation
findings.evidence: `RootLayout` renders `<Navbar />` and `<main>{children}</main>` and nothing after. The homepage ends on the cat grid + "More prints in the darkroom"; /projects ends on the last accordion row's hairline; /contact and /ask end on their last paragraph over the dapple texture. There is no place for the usual "© 2026 Bennett M. Anderson · GitHub · LinkedIn · Email · Source" line, and a visitor at the bottom of a long /projects page has to scroll back up to navigate.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `app/components/Footer.tsx` rendered after `<main>` in layout.tsx: a single hairline-topped row inside `max-width: var(--max-width)`, mono `text-3xs` uppercase on the left (`Bennett M. Anderson · © {new Date().getFullYear()}`) and `TextLink`s on the right (GitHub, LinkedIn, Email from `app/data/site.ts`, plus "Source" → the peninsula repo URL already used in projects.ts:226). Keep it to one row, no columns, to match the restraint of the rest of the design. Owner to confirm wording.

findings.title: Every page's browser tab reads 'B. A.' — no per-page titles
findings.evidence: `metadata.title = "B. A."` is the only title in the app; every route is a `"use client"` page and none exports `metadata`, so /projects, /ask and /contact all show "B. A." in the tab, history, and bookmarks. A recruiter with several candidate tabs open can't tell them apart, and the initials don't match the name shown in the navbar and hero ("Bennett M. Anderson"). (Overlaps with the SEO dimension; listed here for the tab/history experience.)
findings.proposed_fix: In layout.tsx: `title: { default: "Bennett M. Anderson", template: "%s · Bennett M. Anderson" }`. Because the pages are client components, add a tiny `layout.tsx` per route (`app/projects/layout.tsx` etc.) that only does `export const metadata = { title: "Projects" }` and returns `children` — or split each page into a server `page.tsx` that exports metadata and renders the existing client component. Suggested titles: Projects, Ask, Contact, Darkroom, Vault (or "Restricted" for the easter egg).

findings.title: External links open new tabs with no indication; theme toggle label uses design jargon
findings.evidence: `Button` (line 318) and `TextLink` (line 511) add `target="_blank"` to any `http` href, and `RecentPosts` PostCard does the same (RecentPosts.tsx:28). The hero's LinkedIn/GitHub/YouTube/X/Substack buttons (app/page.tsx:172-191), the /projects "View on GitHub"/"Watch on YouTube" links, and the contact rows all leave the site in a new tab with nothing visual or announced — only PostCard has an `ArrowUpRight` glyph. The navbar toggle's `aria-label="Toggle light and dark ground"` (Navbar.tsx:141) uses the design-system word "ground" that no visitor will recognise, and doesn't say which way it will toggle.
findings.proposed_fix: In `Button` and `TextLink`, when `external`, append ` (opens in a new tab)` and, for `TextLink` with `arrow`, render `↗` instead of `→` so the glyph itself signals off-site (the same convention PostCard already uses). Navbar: `aria-label={dark ? "Switch to light theme" : "Switch to dark theme"}` and `title` to match.

findings.title: 'Download resume' forces a download with no way to preview and no file details
findings.evidence: `<Button variant="primary" href={RESUME_PATH} download ...>Download resume</Button>` sets the `download` attribute, so clicking always saves `ResumeBennettAnderson.pdf` (348 KB) to disk; on mobile Safari and in many corporate browsers that's a worse experience than opening the PDF inline, and nothing tells the visitor it's a PDF or how large it is. There's no secondary "view" affordance anywhere on the site, even though the Resume Refresh project shows a preview image on /projects.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the primary button but make it open the PDF (`href={RESUME_PATH}` without `download`, `target="_blank"`) labelled "Resume (PDF)", with a ghost `Button ... download iconLeft={<Download/>}` "Download" beside it — or keep a single download button and change its label to "Download resume · PDF, 348 KB". Owner's preference; either is one-line.

findings.title: Collapsed accordion panels stay in the tab order and triggers lack aria-controls
findings.evidence: Closed panels are hidden only visually (`grid-template-rows: 0fr` + `overflow: hidden`, globals.css:426-437); their content is still mounted, so the "View on GitHub"/"Watch on YouTube" links (projects/page.tsx:80-88) and the lazily-loaded YouTube `<iframe>` (line 66) inside every *closed* project remain focusable. A keyboard user tabbing through /projects lands on invisible links and iframes between the visible rows — with 9 projects that's dozens of hidden stops. The trigger has `aria-expanded` but no `aria-controls`/panel `id`.
findings.proposed_fix: On the `.md-acc-panel` div add `inert={!isOpen}` (React 19 supports the boolean attribute; it removes the subtree from focus and AT) and `id={`${item.id}-panel`}` / `aria-controls` on the trigger, using the stable `id` from the earlier accordion finding. `aria-hidden={!isOpen}` is a fallback for older browsers.
